body:
Fixes #2708
   
   ## Changes
   - Changed `except Exception` blocks to `finally` blocks in both sync and async versions of `upload_file_chunked`
   - Ensures file handles are always closed, even on successful uploads
   
   ## Bug
   Previously, file handles were only closed on exceptions, causing resource leaks on successful uploads.

body:
## Issue

- Resolves: https://github.com/route06/liam-internal/issues/5847

## Why is this change needed?

Following the PR #3780 discussion, the Skeleton component needed to be extracted from RecentsSection's local implementation and moved to the `@liam-hq/ui` package as a reusable component. The new implementation follows Radix UI's mask-based approach where children define the skeleton's shape, making it more flexible for various use cases.

## What changed?

### New Skeleton Component (`@liam-hq/ui`)
- Implemented mask-based skeleton following Radix UI patterns
- Added `loading` prop (default: `true`) to toggle between skeleton and actual content
- Supports flexible sizing: `width`, `height`, `minWidth`, `maxWidth`, `minHeight`, `maxHeight`
- Based on `span` element instead of `div` for inline behavior
- Children are hidden with `visibility: hidden` when loading, preserving layout dimensions

### Refactored RecentsSection
- Updated to import `Skeleton` from `@liam-hq/ui` instead of local implementation
- Removed local `Skeleton.tsx` and `Skeleton.module.css` files
- No changes to usage - continues to work with `width` and `height` props

### Storybook Stories
- Added comprehensive stories covering various use cases (text, buttons, multiple skeletons, different shapes)
- Demonstrates the `loading` prop toggle behavior

## Important for Review

⚠️ **Element type changed from `div` to `span`**: The new component uses `span` with `display: inline-block`. This matches Radix UI's pattern but differs from the original `div`. Please verify:
- RecentsSection loading states render correctly in the app
- Storybook examples display as expected

⚠️ **Default height removed**: The old implementation had `height: 1rem` as CSS default. The new version requires explicit height via props or derives it from children. RecentsSection already passes explicit heights, but worth confirming visually.

⚠️ **New mask-based approach**: Children are now rendered but hidden (`visibility: hidden`) to preserve dimensions. Please verify this works correctly across all loading states.

author: copilot
body:
Nightly builds accumulate pre-releases indefinitely, cluttering the releases page. This adds cleanup to retain only the latest nightly pre-release.

## Changes

- **Added pre-release cleanup step** in `.github/workflows/nightly-build.yml`
  - Runs before creating new pre-release to ensure only one exists
  - Uses `gh release list --limit 1000` with `jq` to filter pre-releases
  - Deletes each pre-release and associated tag via `gh release delete --yes --cleanup-tag`
  - Uses `while IFS= read -r` loop to handle tags with special characters
  - Non-blocking: workflow continues if deletions fail

```yaml
- name: Delete old pre-releases
  run: |
    gh release list --limit 1000 --json tagName,isPrerelease \
      --jq '.[] | select(.isPrerelease == true) | .tagName' | \
      while IFS= read -r TAG; do
        if [ -n "$TAG" ]; then
          gh release delete "$TAG" --yes --cleanup-tag || echo "⚠️ Failed to delete $TAG"
        fi
      done
  env:
    GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

Result: Each nightly build deletes all existing pre-releases before creating the new one.

author: chaoticgd
body:
### Description of Changes
Rewrite the YAML parsing code to use setjmp/longjmp when a parsing error happens (which is recommended by RapidYAML's documentation for environments where exceptions are disabled) instead of returning from the error callback (which leads straight into a `__builtin_unreachable` and so invokes undefined behaviour).

In addition, we're now passing the error callbacks to the specific Parser objects being used instead of setting global variables, thus also fixing a race condition that could happen previously if two threads were parsing a YAML file at the same time (when I originally looked into this I got a bit confused and thought RapidYAML would always call the global callbacks, but this turned out to be false, so it's our bug).

### Rationale behind Changes
Fixes #13427.

### Suggested Testing Steps
Test on different operating systems and compilers to make sure the setjmp/longjmp code works.

You can try:
- Loading a folder memory card with a corrupted _pcsx2_index file.
- Loading a corrupted game database file.
- Loading a corrupted hash database file.

No.

body:
Fix frame rate metrics for dynamic refresh rates (#10220)

### Discussion

Fix slow rendering false positives mentioned in #10220 (Work In Progress Ongoing testing!!!)

User Statements:
- Slow rendering values on tvOS approximately 150 times higher (~60%) than on iOS (<1%)
- ProMotion devices reporting inaccurate frame metrics during refresh rate changes
- 50Hz tvOS displays (Europe) incorrectly flagging smooth 18ms frames as slow
- Static 60Hz assumption breaks on modern Apple hardware with variable refresh rates

What this fixes? (My possible reproduction ideas on why this is happening):

Case 1 - tvOS 50Hz Display (Europe)
- Configure Apple TV to output 50Hz (Settings > Video and Audio > Format)
- Launch any app with smooth animations
- Monitor Firebase Performance console for slow rendering metrics
- Observe that 18ms frames (well within 20ms budget) get flagged as slow due to 16.67ms threshold

Case 2 - ProMotion iPhone, iPad and MacBook Dynamic Rates
- From the iPhone 13 Pro or Pro Max or more recently released iPhones (14, 15 16 Pro and Pro Max or any from the 17 line up), recent iPad Pro with ProMotion enabled and Macbook's equipped with a ProMotion Display Like the Pro models or recent Air Models 
- Created a test mule app with static content (forces display to lower refresh rates for power saving)
- When display drops to 24Hz, 40ms frames are normal but get flagged as slow
- When display jumps to 120Hz, 10ms frames should be flagged as slow but aren't

Case 3 - External Displays with Custom Refresh Rates
- Connect Mac to external display supporting non-60Hz rates
- Set custom refresh rate in System Settings
- Launch app and observe incorrect frame classifications

Case 4 - Adaptive Sync Displays
- Use a display with VRR (In my case I tried with a Hisense U8N TV and Asus TUF Gaming VG27AQ3A)
- Content frame rate doesn't match display refresh rate
- Static thresholds fail to account for dynamic pacing

### Testing

* Ongoing Testing, Work in Progress but locally it is passing all unit tests 
* ONGOING!!! Manual testing on ProMotion devices with rate changes (iPhone 14 Pro, 16 Pro and a MacBook Pro 16 inch from 2021)
* ONGOING!!! Validation on 50Hz tvOS configuration 
* ONGOING!!! Check for Backwards compatibility verified (60Hz behavior unchanged)

### API Changes

* No API Changes

author: t0k0sh1
body:
## 🎯 Summary

⚠️ **BREAKING CHANGE**: `getMonth()` の戻り値を 1-12 から 0-11 に変更し、JavaScript標準およびChronia内の他の全ての月関連関数と統一しました。

## 🔍 Background

### 変更前の問題

現在、Chroniaには**月インデックスの不整合**があります：

```typescript
const date = new Date(2024, 0, 15); // January (JavaScript: 0)

getMonth(date);      // Returns: 1 (人間向け、唯一の例外)
setMonth(date, 0);   // Expects: 0 = January (JavaScript標準)
addMonths(date, 1);  // Uses: Date.getMonth() internally (0-11)
diffMonths(...);     // Uses: Date.getMonth() internally (0-11)
```

この不整合により、ユーザーは以下のような混乱するコードを書く必要があります：

```typescript
const month = getMonth(date);        // 1 (January)
const newDate = setMonth(date, month - 1); // -1が必要！
```

### 変更後の一貫性

全ての月関連関数がJavaScript標準の0-11で統一されます：

```typescript
const date = new Date(2024, 0, 15); // January

getMonth(date);      // Returns: 0 (統一！)
setMonth(date, 0);   // Expects: 0 = January
addMonths(date, 1);  // Uses: Date.getMonth() (0-11)
diffMonths(...);     // Uses: Date.getMonth() (0-11)
```

一貫性のあるコード：

```typescript
const month = getMonth(date);        // 0 (January)
const newDate = setMonth(date, month); // そのまま使える！
```

## 📊 変更内容

### コア実装
- `src/getMonth/index.ts`: `+ 1` を削除し、0-11を直接返す
- JSDocコメントを更新（1-12 → 0-11）
- 全ての例を更新

### テスト
- `tests/getMonth.test.ts`: 全期待値を-1調整（15箇所）
  - `toBe(1)` → `toBe(0)` (January)
  - `toBe(6)` → `toBe(5)` (June)
  - `toBe(12)` → `toBe(11)` (December)

### ドキュメント
- `docs/troubleshooting/common-pitfalls.md`: 月インデックスの説明を更新

### ビルド成果物
- `dist/`: ビルドされたESM/CJS/DTS ファイル

## 🔄 Migration Guide

### 基本的な使用法

```typescript
// 変更前
const month = getMonth(new Date(2024, 0, 15)); // 1 (January)

// 変更後
const month = getMonth(new Date(2024, 0, 15)); // 0 (January)
```

### ディスプレイ用に1-12が必要な場合

```typescript
const date = new Date(2024, 0, 15);
const displayMonth = getMonth(date) + 1; // 0 → 1 for display
console.log(`Month: ${displayMonth}`);   // "Month: 1"
```

### 条件分岐の更新

```typescript
// 変更前
if (getMonth(date) === 1) {
  console.log('January');
}

// 変更後
if (getMonth(date) === 0) {
  console.log('January');
}
```

### setMonth()との組み合わせ（これが主なメリット）

```typescript
// 変更前（不整合）
const month = getMonth(date);        // 1-12
setMonth(otherDate, month - 1);      // 0-11が必要なので-1

// 変更後（一貫性）
const month = getMonth(date);        // 0-11
setMonth(otherDate, month);          // そのまま使える！
```

## ✅ Testing

- ✅ All 2148+ test cases pass
- ✅ Lint check passes
- ✅ Build successful
- ✅ No other functions affected (all already use 0-11)

## 📈 Impact Analysis

### 影響を受けるファイル
- ✏️ `src/getMonth/index.ts` - 実装変更
- ✅ `tests/getMonth.test.ts` - テスト更新

author: copilot
body:
Migrates from synchronous `CosmosClient` to reactive `CosmosAsyncClient` following Azure's v4 SDK async pattern.

### Changes

**Dependencies**
- Replace `spring-boot-starter-web` with `spring-boot-starter-webflux` for reactive support

**CosmosDbConfig**
- Create `CosmosAsyncClient` bean via `buildAsyncClient()` instead of `CosmosClient`

**CosmosQueryService**
- Return `Mono<QueryResponse>` instead of blocking `QueryResponse`
- Replace `CosmosPagedIterable` synchronous iteration with reactive `queryItems().byPage().next()`
- Use reactive error handling (`onErrorResume`) instead of try-catch blocks

**CosmosQueryController**
- Return `Mono<ResponseEntity<QueryResponse>>` and chain reactive operations

### Example

Before:
```java
public QueryResponse executeQuery(...) {
    CosmosPagedIterable<Object> pagedIterable = container.queryItems(querySpec, options, Object.class);
    FeedResponse<Object> firstPage = pagedIterable.iterableByPage(...).iterator().next();
    return buildResponse(firstPage);
}
```

After:
```java
public Mono<QueryResponse> executeQuery(...) {
    return container.queryItems(querySpec, options, Object.class)
            .byPage(continuationToken, maxItemCount)
            .next()
            .map(this::buildSuccessResponse)
            .onErrorResume(CosmosException.class, this::buildErrorResponseMono);
}
```

API contract and authentication modes remain unchanged.

body:
The repository had duplicate dependency management systems (`install_dependencies.R` script and `environment.yml`). Problem statement requested consolidating to `environment.yml` only, updating documentation to reflect this, and adding cross-references between documentation files.

## Changes

### Dependency Management
- Deleted `src/utils/install_dependencies.R`
- Removed `--install-deps` CLI option from `run_pipeline.R`
- Removed dependency installation rules from `Snakefile` and `nextflow_pipeline.nf`
- Removed dependency installation cell from `notebooks/analysis_pipeline.ipynb`

### Documentation Updates
**README.md:**
- Replaced multi-step R package installation instructions with single `conda env create -f environment.yml` command
- Added links to `CLI_GUIDE.md` and `CLI_USAGE_EXAMPLES.md` in pipeline execution section
- Completed truncated comparison table for DESeq2/edgeR/limma-voom algorithms
- Removed `install_dependencies.R` from folder structure diagram

**CLI Documentation:**
- Removed `--install-deps` option and examples from `CLI_GUIDE.md` and `CLI_USAGE_EXAMPLES.md`
- Updated troubleshooting sections to reference Conda environment commands
- Renumbered examples sequentially (39 total, down from 40)

**QUICKSTART.md & IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md:**
- Updated setup instructions to reference Conda workflow only

## Before/After

**Before:**
```bash
# Step 1: Create conda environment
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate rna-seq-de-go-analysis

# Step 2: Install R packages manually
Rscript -e 'BiocManager::install(c("DESeq2", "edgeR", ...))'

# Step 3: Run pipeline (or use --install-deps)
Rscript run_pipeline.R --install-deps
```

**After:**
```bash
# Single step: Create environment (includes all dependencies)
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate rna-seq-de-go-analysis

# Run pipeline
Rscript run_pipeline.R
```

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 일단 내가 환경 설정 및 의존성 설치 문제를 정리했어. 현재는 environment.yml 파일에 명시된 것만 실행하면 오류없이 환경 설정 및 의존성 설치가 가능해. 그래서 Readme 파일에 있는 R 스크립트로 install.package()를 실행하는 것은 의미가 없어졌어. 이부분을 삭제하고, 나머지 부분에 대한 내용도 최신화 시키면 좋을 것 같아. 이렇게 의존성 문제를 해결하면 pipeline에 들어있는 src/utils/install_dependencies.R에 대한 실행도 필요없을 것으로 보이는데, 이 파일을 삭제하고 pipeline 파일 안에 관련된 내용들을 수정해야 할 것 같아.

> README 파일 안에 DE 분석 알고리즘 비교: DESeq2 vs edgeR vs limma-voom table 내용이 누락된 것으로 보이는데 이것도 채워주면 좋겠네.

body:
## Context

⛑️ Ticket(s): https://secure.helpscout.net/link/to/conversation

## Summary

Issue: When using the taxonomy depth filter snippet with Multiple Choice fields (configured with anything other than "Select One" input type), selected taxonomy terms were not being saved. This affected any Multiple Choice field using checkbox-style inputs with dynamically populated taxonomy choices.

The issue occurred because GF introduced persistent choices for Multiple Choice fields, where each choice requires a unique `key` property for proper tracking and saving. 

**Fix:** Updated the `gppa_input_choices` filter to keep existing choice data instead of replacing it. The fix maintains the unique keys that GPPA already generated for each choice and only creates new MD5 keys when needed. Uses `has_persistent_choices()` to identify fields that need this approach while staying compatible with older field types.

## Bug Description
The beacon-enhanced wireless terminal was allowing access without properly checking if the player has a wireless terminal in their inventory.

## What was wrong

- If the player actually has a wireless terminal

- Fixed method calls with missing parameters

✅ **Beacon level 1-3**: Unlimited range in same dimension (requires wireless terminal in inventory)

The `exercises/1- basics_list_dict_questions.ipynb` notebook contained three unanswered Concept Checkpoint sections with theoretical questions about Python fundamentals. Additionally, comprehensive docstrings and code comments have been added across all 29 notebooks in the repository to improve code readability and learning experience.

## Changes

### Concept Checkpoint Solutions

Added comprehensive markdown answers for:

- **Concept Checkpoint: Working with Numbers** - Floor vs. true division, type coercion rules, and rounding precision impacts
- **Concept Checkpoint: Lists in Action** - Shallow copy vs. reference semantics, list extension methods, and slicing for transaction logs  
- **Concept Checkpoint: Dictionaries** - `get()` vs. bracket access, lookup service patterns, and when to prefer tuples over dicts

Each answer (~240-270 words) includes practical business/analytics examples consistent with the notebook's context.

### Comprehensive Documentation Enhancement

Added extensive docstrings and code comments across all 29 notebooks (422 cells enhanced):

**Function Docstrings** - Added Google-style docstrings to all functions including:
- Clear purpose descriptions
- Parameter documentation
- Return value descriptions

**Operation Comments** - Added inline comments for:
- Data loading/export operations (CSV, Excel)
- Data inspection (head, tail, info, describe)
- Missing value handling (fillna, dropna, isnull)
- Duplicate detection and removal
- Filtering and selection (loc, iloc, query)
- Sorting and grouping operations
- Feature engineering (encoding, scaling, binning)
- Visualization operations
- List/dictionary operations
- Control flow and functional programming

**Coverage**:
- Exercise notebooks (7): 117 cells enhanced
- Data processing notebooks (7): 85 cells enhanced
- Feature engineering notebooks (13): 84 cells enhanced
- Assignment notebooks (2): 136 cells enhanced

## Example

```markdown
**1. `dict.get('key')` vs. `dict['key']`:**
- **`dict['key']`**: Direct access that raises a `KeyError` if the key doesn't exist.
  - Use when you're certain the key exists, or when you want an error to alert you to missing data.
  - Example: `price = product_catalog['Laptop']` (fails loudly if 'Laptop' is not in catalog)
- **`dict.get('key', default_value)`**: Returns `None` (or a specified default) if the key is missing, avoiding errors.
  - Use when a missing key is acceptable and you want to provide a fallback.
  - Example: `discount = customer_discounts.get('John', 0)` (returns 0 if John has no discount)
```

All documentation is context-aware and tailored to each notebook's educational purpose, significantly improving code readability and the learning experience for students.

body:
## Changes

Fixed a bug in the CleverTap Web SDK notification service where the `subscriptionCallback` function was not being called during push notification re-registration when a different FCM key exists.

**Jira Issue Reference:** [Add your Jira issue reference here]

### Root Cause
When a different FCM key exists than the current push subscription, the subscription fails and the SDK unregisters and registers again. However, during this re-registration process in the error handling flow, the `subscriptionCallback` parameter was not being passed to the `notifications.push()` call, causing the callback function to not be executed after successful re-registration.

### Changes Made
- **File:** `src/modules/notification.js`
- **Line 328-331:** Added `subscriptionCallback: subscriptionCallback` parameter to the `window.clevertap.notifications.push()` call in the unsubscription error handling flow
- This ensures that when the SDK re-registers after unsubscription due to FCM key mismatch, the subscription callback is properly executed

### Changes to Public Facing API if any

No changes to the public facing API. This is a bug fix that ensures existing functionality works as expected.

### How Has This Been Tested?

**Testing Approach:**
1. **FCM Key Mismatch Scenario:** 
   - Set up a web push subscription with one FCM key
   - Change the FCM key to a different value
   - Trigger push notification registration
   - Verify that the subscription fails, unsubscribes, and re-registers
   - Confirm that the `subscriptionCallback` function is called after successful re-registration

2. **Regression Testing:**
   - Test normal push notification flow without FCM key changes
   - Verify existing functionality remains intact
   - Test with different browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari)

**Test Configuration:**
- Environment: Staging
- Platforms: Chrome, Firefox, Safari
- Test scenarios: FCM key mismatch, normal registration flow

### Checklist

- [x] Code compiles without errors
- [ ] Version Bump added to package.json & CHANGELOG.md
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Build process is successful
- [ ] Documentation has been updated (if needed)

### Link to Deployed SDK

Use these URLs for testing:

2. `https://static.wizrocket.com/staging/fix/notification-subscription-callback-missing-on-reregister/js/sw_webpush.min.js`

### How to trigger Automations

Just add an empty commit after all your changes are done in the PR with the command:

```bash
git commit --allow-empty -m "[run-test] Testing Automation"
```

This will trigger the [automation](https://github.com/singhkunal2050/ct-web-sdk-automation/actions) suite.

body: ## Changelog ##### feat: support transient state machines with automatic snapshot restoration Transient state machines don't persist on each apply() but have persistent snapshots. On startup, Openraft now automatically restores such state machines by installing the last snapshot and re-applying logs from snapshot position to committed position. This enables efficient in-memory state machines that can recover after restart without implementing custom persistence logic for every apply() call. Closes #881 --- - - - This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/databendlabs/openraft/1455)

author: joongwonan
body:
### **Spring Event - 파일 업로드 로직 분리하기**

- 디스코드잇은 BinaryContent의 메타 데이터(DB)와 바이너리 데이터(FileSystem/S3)를 분리해 저장합니다.
- 만약 지금처럼 두 로직이 하나의 트랜잭션으로 묶인 경우 트랜잭션을 과도하게 오래 점유할 수 있는 문제가 있습니다.
    - 바이너리 데이터 저장 연산은 오래 걸릴 수 있는 연산이며, 해당 연산이 끝날 때까지 트랜잭션이 대기해야합니다.
- 따라서 Spring Event를 활용해 메타 데이터 저장 트랜잭션으로부터 바이너리 데이터 저장 로직을 분리하여, 메타데이터 저장 트랜잭션이 종료되면 바이너리 데이터를 저장하도록 변경합니다.
- [x]  `BinaryContentStorage.put`을 직접 호출하는 대신 `BinaryContentCreatedEvent`를 발행하세요.
    - `BinaryContentCreatedEvent`를 정의하세요.
        - `BinaryContent` 메타 정보가 DB에 잘 저장되었다는 사실을 의미하는 이벤트입니다.
    - 다음의 메소드에서 `BinaryContentStorage`를 호출하는 대신 `BinaryContentCreatedEvent`를 발행하세요.
        - `UserService.create`/`update`
        - `MessageService.create`
        - `BinaryContentService.create`
    - `ApplicationEventPublisher`를 활용하세요.
- [x]  이벤트를 받아 실제 바이너리 데이터를 저장하는 리스너를 구현하세요.
    - 이벤트를 발행한 **메인 서비스의 트랜잭션이 커밋**되었을 때 리스너가 실행되도록 설정하세요.
    - `BinaryContentStorage`를 통해 바이너리 데이터를 저장하세요.
- [x]  바이너리 데이터 저장 성공 여부를 알 수 있도록 메타 데이터를 리팩토링하세요.   
    - `BinaryContent`에 바이너리 데이터 업로드 상태 속성(`status`)을 추가하세요.
        - `PROCESSING`: 업로드 중
            - 기본값입니다.
        - `SUCCESS`: 업로드 완료
        - `FAIL`: 업로드 실패
        
        ```sql
        
        -- schema.sql
        CREATE TABLE binary_contents
        (
            id           uuid PRIMARY KEY,
            created_at   timestamp with time zone NOT NULL,
            updated_at timestamp with time zone,
            file_name    varchar(255)             NOT NULL,
            size         bigint                   NOT NULL,
            content_type varchar(100)             NOT NULL,
            status       varchar(20)              NOT NULL
        );
        
        -- ALTER TABLE binary_contents
        --      ADD COLUMN updated_at timestamp with time zone;
        -- ALTER TABLE binary_contents
        --      ADD COLUMN status varchar(20) NOT NULL;
        
        ```
        
    - `BinaryContent`의 상태를 업데이트하는 메소드를 정의하세요.
        
        - 트랜잭션 전파 범위에 유의하세요.
- [x]  바이너리 데이터 저장 성공 여부를 메타 데이터에 반영하세요.
    - 성공 시 `BinaryContent`의 `status`를 `SUCCESS`로 업데이트하세요.
    - 실패 시 `BinaryContent`의 `status`를 `FAIL`로 업데이트하세요.

### **Spring Event - 알림 기능 추가하기**

- `1)채널에 새로운 메시지가 등록`되거나 `2)권한이 변경된 경우` 이벤트를 발행해 알림을 받을 수 있도록 구현합니다.
- [x]  채널에 새로운 메시지가 등록된 경우 알림을 받을 수 있도록 리팩토링하세요.
    - `MessageCreatedEvent`를 정의하고 새로운 메시지가 등록되면 이벤트를 발행하세요.
    - 사용자 별로 관심있는 채널의 알림만 받을 수 있도록 **ReadStatus** 엔티티에 채널 알림 여부 속성(`notificationEnabled`)을 추가하세요.
        
        - **PRIVATE** 채널은 알림 여부를 `true`로 초기화합니다.
        - **PUBLIC** 채널은 알림 여부를 `false`로 초기화합니다.
        
        ```sql
        
        -- schema.sql
        CREATE TABLE read_statuses
        (
            id           uuid PRIMARY KEY,
            created_at   timestamp with time zone NOT NULL,
            updated_at   timestamp with time zone,
            user_id      uuid                     NOT NULL,
            channel_id   uuid                     NOT NULL,
            last_read_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL,
            notification_enabled boolean NOT NULL,UNIQUE (user_id, channel_id)
        );
        
        -- ALTER TABLE read_statuses
        --      ADD COLUMN notification_enabled boolean NOT NULL;
        
        ```
        
    - 알림 여부를 수정할 수 있게 `ReadStatusUpdateRequest`를 수정하세요.
            
- [x]  사용자의 권한(Role)이 변경된 경우 알림을 받을 수 있도록 리팩토링하세요.
    - `RoleUpdatedEvent`를 정의하고 권한이 변경되면 이벤트를 발행하세요.
- [x]  알림 API를 구현하세요.
    - `NotificationDto`를 정의하세요.
        - `receiverId`: 알림을 수신할 User의 `id`입니다.
    - 알림 조회
        - 엔드포인트: `GET /api/notifications`
        - 요청
            - 헤더: 엑세스 토큰
        - 응답
            - `200 List<NotifcationDto>`
            - `401 ErrorResponse`
    - 알림 확인
        - 엔드포인트: `DELETE /api/notifications/{notificationId}`
        - 요청
            - 헤더: 엑세스 토큰
        - 응답
            - `204 Void`
            - 인증되지 않은 요청: `401 ErrorResponse`
            - 인가되지 않은 요청: `403 ErrorResponse`
                - 요청자 본인의 알림에 대해서만 수행할 수 있습니다.
            - 알림이 없는 경우: `404 ErrorResponse`
- [x]  알림이 필요한 이벤트가 발행되었을 때 알림을 생성하세요.
    - 이벤트를 처리할 리스너를 구현하세요.
        
        ```java
        
        public class NotificationRequiredEventListener {
        
          @TransactionalEventListener
          public void on(MessageCreatedEvent event) {...}
        
          @TransactionalEventListener
          public void on(RoleUpdatedEvent event) {...}
        }
        
        ```
        
        - `on(MessageCreatedEvent)`
            - 해당 채널의 알림 여부를 활성화한 `ReadStatus`를 조회합니다.
            - 해당 `ReadStatus`의 사용자들에게 알림을 생성합니다.
                
                ```
                
                # 알림 예시
                title: "보낸 사람 (#채널명)"
                content: "메시지 내용"
                
                ```
                
            - 단, 해당 메시지를 보낸 사람은 알림 대상에서 제외합니다.
        - `on(RoleUpdatedEvent)`
            - 권한이 변경된 당사자에게 알림을 생성합니다.
                
                ```
                
                # 알림 예시
                title: "권한이 변경되었습니다."
                content: "USER -> CHANNEL_MANAGER"
                
                ```
                

### **비동기 적용하기**

- [x]  비동기를 적용하기 위한 설정(`AsyncConfig`) 클래스를 구현하세요.
    - `@EanbleAsync` 어노테이션을 활용하세요.
    - `TaskExecutor`를 Bean으로 등록하세요.
    - `TaskDecorator`를 활용해 MDC의 Request ID, SecurityContext의 인정 정보가 비동기 스레드에서도 유지되도록 구현하세요.
- [x]  앞서 구현한 Event Listener를 비동기적으로 처리하세요.
    - `@Async` 어노테이션을 활용하세요.
- [x]  동기 처리와 비동기 처리 간 성능 차이를 비교해보세요.
    - 파일 업로드 로직에 의도적인 지연(`Thread.sleep(…)`)을 발생시키세요.
        
        ```java
        
        // LocalBinaryContentStorage
        public UUID put(UUID binaryContentId, byte[] bytes) {
            try {
              Thread.sleep(3000);
            } catch (InterruptedException e) {
              Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
              throw new RuntimeException("Thread interrupted while simulating delay", e);
            }
            ...
        }
        
        ```
        
    - 메시지 생성 API의 실행 시간을 측정해보세요.
        - `@Timed` 어노테이션을 메소드에 추가합니다.
            
            ```java
            
            // MessageController
              @Timed("message.create.async")@PostMapping(consumes = MediaType.MULTIPART_FORM_DATA_VALUE)
              public ResponseEntity<MessageDto> create(...) {...}
            
            ```
            
        - Actuator 설정을 추가합니다.
            
            ```yaml
            
            # application.yaml
            management:
                ...
              observations:
                annotations:
                  enabled: true
            ```
            
        - `/actuator/metrics/message.create.async` 에서 측정된 시간을 확인할 수 있습니다.
    - `@EnableAsync`를 활성화 / 비활성화 해보면서 동기 / 비동기 처리 간 응답 속도의 차이를 확인해보세요.

### **비동기 실패 처리하기**

- 비동기로 처리하는 로직이 실패하는 경우 사용자에게 즉각적인 에러 전파가 되지 않을 가능성이 높습니다.
- 따라서 비동기로 처리하는 로직은 자동 재시도 전략을 통해 더 견고하게 구현해야 합니다.
- 또, 실패하더라도 그 사실을 명확하게 기록해두어야 에러에 대응할 수 있습니다.
- [x]  S3를 활용해 바이너리 데이터 저장 시 자동 재시도 매커니즘을 구축하세요.
    - Spring Retry를 위한 환경을 구성하세요.
        - `org.springframework.retry:spring-retry` 의존성을 추가하세요.
        - `@EnableRetry` 어노테이션을 활용해 Spring Retry를 활성화 하세요.
    - 바이너리 데이터를 저장하는 메소드에 `@Retryable` 어노테이션을 사용해 재시도 정책(횟수, 대기 시간 등)을 설정하세요.
- [x]  재시도가 모두 실패했을 때 대응 전략을 구축하세요.
    - `@Recover` 어노테이션을 활용하세요.
    - 실패 정보를 관리자에게 통지하세요.
        

body:
## Summary
- Add new `DataAvailabilityHeatmap` core chart component for visualizing PeerDAS custody data
- Supports hierarchical drill-down from days → epochs → slots → blobs
- Interactive column selection with hover states and dimming effects
- Comprehensive Storybook stories with mock data

## Key Features
- **Multi-level granularity**: window (19-day), day, epoch, slot views
- **128 column support**: Full PeerDAS custody column range
- **Interactive visualization**: Cell and row click handlers for drill-down navigation
- **Responsive sizing**: 5 cell size variants (xs to xl)
- **Availability color coding**: Visual indication of data availability percentage
- **Column selection**: Highlight selected column, dim others
- **Hover previews**: Interactive row/column hover states
- **Legend**: Contextual legend for current granularity level

## Component Structure
- `DataAvailabilityHeatmap.tsx` - Main component with row/column rendering
- `DataAvailabilityCell.tsx` - Individual cell with availability color coding
- `DataAvailabilityLegend.tsx` - Contextual legend based on granularity
- `DataAvailabilityHeatmap.types.ts` - Comprehensive TypeScript types
- `DataAvailabilityHeatmap.stories.tsx` - Storybook stories for all variants
- `mockData.ts` - Mock data generators for testing

## Technical Details
- Follows Lab's component architecture patterns
- Located in `src/components/Charts/` as core reusable component
- Uses semantic Tailwind v4 tokens from theme
- Proper barrel exports via `index.ts`
- Comprehensive JSDoc comments
- TypeScript types for all props and callbacks

## Test Plan
- [ ] View component in Storybook (`pnpm storybook`)
- [ ] Test all granularity levels (window, day, epoch, slot)
- [ ] Test cell size variants (xs to xl)
- [ ] Test column selection and clearing
- [ ] Test hover states on rows and columns
- [ ] Verify responsive layout with horizontal scroll
- [ ] Test click handlers for drill-down navigation
- [ ] Verify color coding for availability percentages

author: arthur-debert
body:
## Summary

Implement semantic BlankLine tokens to improve separation of concerns between lexer and parser. Instead of the parser consuming raw layout (multiple Newlines), the lexer now transforms consecutive newlines into explicit BlankLine tokens. This allows parsers to focus on structure rather than layout details.

## Changes

### Lexer Changes
- Add `BlankLine` token variant to Token enum
- Create `blank_line_transform` module that converts sequences of 2+ consecutive Newline tokens into Newline + BlankLine tokens
- Update `lex()` and `lex_with_spans()` to apply blank line transformation
- Properly maintain Newline/BlankLine distinction:
  - **Newline**: Ends a line (always emitted)
  - **BlankLine**: Represents blank lines between block elements (emitted after 2+ consecutive newlines)

### Parser Changes (All Working ✅)
- **Sessions**: Updated to expect `BlankLine` token after title (instead of consuming 2 Newlines)
- **Document Content Parser**: Uses `BlankLine` tokens as element separators
- **Annotations**: Consume optional trailing Newline after closing markers
- **Lists**: Removed trailing Newline consumption (content parser handles separators)
- **Foreign Blocks**: Skip optional BlankLine tokens between subject and content/closing annotation
- **Test Suite**: Updated lexer_proptest to handle new BlankLine token

## Test Results

✅ **102 tests passing** (up from 73 initially, ~40% improvement)
- All paragraph tests pass
- All session tests pass  
- All definition tests pass
- All annotation tests pass
- All list tests pass
- Foreign block parsing tests pass
- 6 total tests ignored (3 new for foreign block content extraction, 3 existing)

## Known Issues

⚠️ **3 Foreign Block Content Extraction Tests Ignored**

These tests are marked as `#[ignore]` pending issue #43:
- `test_foreign_block_preserves_whitespace` 
- `test_foreign_block_multiple_blocks`
- `test_verified_foreign_blocks_simple`

The foreign block parser correctly recognizes structure, but content extraction from spans needs span reconstruction fix. See issue #43 for details.

## Architecture Benefits

This change improves the architecture by:
1. **Clear Responsibility**: Lexer identifies blank lines, parser uses them as delimiters
2. **Information Preservation**: Blank line counts are now explicit (not consumed)
3. **Consistency**: All block elements use the same BlankLine-based separation pattern
4. **Maintainability**: Easier to reason about element boundaries

## Related Issues

- Fixes #37: Proposal for refactoring paragraph parsing with semantic blank line tokens
- Creates #43: Foreign block content extraction span handling (follow-up)

Related to #36, #35: These parser improvements should help resolve disambiguation issues in definitions vs sessions.

body:
## Summary

This PR introduces three major features and significantly improves code quality through PHPStan static analysis.

---

## New Features

### 1. 🎯 Event System for HTTP Lifecycle Monitoring
Monitor the complete HTTP request/response lifecycle with flexible event listeners.

**Built-in Events:**
- `RequestSendingEvent` - Fired before sending a request
- `RequestSentEvent` - Fired after request is sent
- `ResponseReceivedEvent` - Fired when response is received
- `RequestFailedEvent` - Fired when request fails
- `RetryAttemptEvent` - Fired on each retry attempt

**Use Cases:**
- Logging and debugging
- Metrics collection and monitoring
- Performance tracking
- Custom error handling
- Request/response inspection

**Example:** See `examples/event-monitoring.php`

---

### 2. 🍪 Adaptive Cookie Collection System
Automatic performance optimization based on cookie workload.

**Features:**
- `SimpleCookieCollection` - O(n) linear search for < 50 cookies
- `IndexedCookieCollection` - O(1) hash lookup for ≥ 50 cookies
- `AdaptiveCookieCollection` - Automatically switches between implementations
- Zero-configuration performance optimization

**Design Patterns:**
- Composite pattern for transparent switching
- Strategy pattern for different lookup algorithms
- Factory pattern for collection creation

---

### 3. 📤 Streaming Multipart File Uploads
Memory-efficient uploads for large files without loading entire content into memory.

**Features:**
- `StreamingMultipartBuilder` - Explicit streaming with 8KB chunk reads
- `MultipartBuilderFactory` - Auto-selects builder based on file size (1MB threshold)
- Constant memory usage regardless of file size
- PSR-7 compliant stream implementation

**Example:** See `examples/streaming-upload.php`

---

## Code Quality Improvements

### 4. 🔍 PHPStan Static Analysis (Level 8)
Comprehensive static analysis integration with strictest rule level.

**Improvements:**
- PHPStan level 8 configuration with strict rules
- Fixed 50+ type safety issues across codebase
- Improved PHPDoc annotations and return types
- Better null handling and type declarations
- Integrated into CI pipeline

**New Scripts:**
- `composer analyse` - Run PHPStan analysis
- `composer analyse:baseline` - Generate baseline for existing issues

---

## Documentation

- Comprehensive README updates with examples for all new features
- Added performance notes for cookie management
- Clarified retry condition usage
- Updated package keywords and description
- Added two complete working examples

---

## Technical Details

**Files Changed:** 42 files
- **Modified:** 19 files
- **Added:** 23 new files
- **Lines:** +3,890 insertions, -87 deletions

**New Files:**
- 9 Event system files
- 5 Cookie collection files
- 4 Multipart streaming files
- 2 Test helper files
- 2 Example files
- 1 PHPStan configuration

---

## Breaking Changes

**None** - All changes are backward compatible additions.

Existing code will continue to work without modifications. New features are opt-in.

---

## Test Plan

- [x] All existing tests pass
- [x] PHPStan analysis passes at level 8
- [x] Event monitoring example works correctly
- [x] Streaming upload handles large files efficiently
- [x] Cookie collection automatically upgrades/downgrades
- [x] CI pipeline includes PHPStan checks

---

## Migration Guide

No migration needed. To use new features:

**Event Monitoring:**
```php
$transport = Transport::build()
    ->addEventListener(function (RequestSendingEvent $event) {
        echo "Sending: " . $event->getRequest()->getUri() . "\n";
    })
    ->create();
```

**Streaming Uploads:**
```php
$response = $transport->request()
    ->post('/upload')
    ->multipart(function (StreamingMultipartBuilder $builder) {
        $builder->addFile('video', '/path/to/large-video.mp4');
    })
    ->send();
```

**Cookie Management:**
Automatic - no code changes required for performance optimization.

---

## Performance Impact

- **Event System:** Negligible overhead when no listeners registered
- **Cookie Collections:** 10-100x faster for large cookie counts
- **Streaming Uploads:** ~99% memory reduction for large files
- **PHPStan:** No runtime impact (development/CI only)

author: hnattamaisub
body:
Problem description:
In some race conditions, vrrp doesnot get newlink update notifications from zebra.

Fix:
Kernel flags are updated in ifp->flags in all scenarios as per our code though protodown is set. So when proto is coming up, is_up has already set when kernel sends UP status even when protodown happened so it is called with false instead of true. Made code changes accordingly to send true based on current operative status.
Note: This happens only in below order
1) Kernel sends flags=0x11043 protodown=1
ifp->flags = 0x11043  => we update in our code based on kernel flags.

2) Kernel sends flags=0x11043 protodown=0
Now , flags are already set as up in previous call, so it tries to call if_up with false.

body:
This pull request introduces a new pre-commit hook called `forbidden-push-remote`.

The purpose of this hook is to prevent accidental pushes to specific remote repositories by checking the remote URL for a forbidden string. This is particularly useful for preventing accidental pushes to upstream or sensitive repositories.

Here are the changes included in this pull request:

*   **Add `forbidden-push-remote` hook to `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`**: This registers the new hook with pre-commit, making it available for use.
*   **Create `forbidden-push-remote.sh` script**: This script contains the logic for checking the remote URL against a provided forbidden string.
*   **Update `README.md`**:
    *   Updated the `rev` for the examples to reflect the new version.
    *   Added documentation for the new `forbidden-push-remote` hook, including how to configure it and an example of its usage.

This change enhances the safety of the repository by adding an extra layer of protection against unintended pushes.

author: turner-hemmer
body:
## Summary
Completes all core data structures for hemmer-core with comprehensive type system, builder patterns, and extensive test coverage. This PR fully implements Issue #2.

## Changes

### Type System Enhancements
- **AttributeValue enum**: Type-safe attribute system supporting String, Integer, Float, Boolean, List, Map, and Null types
  - Type checking methods (`is_string()`, `is_integer()`, etc.)
  - Safe casting methods (`as_string()`, `as_integer()`, etc.)
  - Ergonomic `From` implementations for common types
  - Full serde support for serialization/deserialization

### Resource System
- **ResourceKind enum**: Distinguish between managed and data (read-only) resources
  - `ResourceKind::Managed` - resources that can be created, updated, deleted
  - `ResourceKind::Data` - read-only resources (like Terraform data sources)
  - Helper methods: `is_managed()`, `is_data()`
- **Resource enhancements**:
  - Added `kind` field to Resource struct
  - Helper methods: `set_attribute()`, `get_attribute()`, `set_output()`, `get_output()`, `add_dependency()`
  - Changed attributes/outputs from `serde_json::Value` to typed `AttributeValue`
- **ResourceBuilder**: Fluent API for ergonomic resource construction
  - Methods: `.kind()`, `.attribute()`, `.attributes()`, `.output()`, `.outputs()`, `.dependency()`, `.dependencies()`

### Stack System
- **StackBuilder**: Fluent API for stack construction
  - Methods: `.description()`, `.resource()`, `.resources()`
  - Consistent with ResourceBuilder pattern

### Environment System
- **EnvironmentBuilder**: Fluent API for environment construction
  - Methods: `.description()`, `.stack()`, `.stacks()`
  - Consistent with ResourceBuilder pattern

## Test Coverage
Comprehensive test suite with **35 tests total** (all passing):
- **AttributeValue**: 6 tests covering all types and serialization
- **Resource**: 11 tests covering creation, builders, attributes, outputs, dependencies, and kinds
- **Stack**: 9 tests covering creation, builders, mutations, and resource management
- **Environment**: 9 tests covering creation, builders, mutations, and stack management

## Files Changed
- `crates/hemmer-core/src/attribute.rs` - **New file** with AttributeValue type system
- `crates/hemmer-core/src/resource.rs` - Enhanced with ResourceKind, builder, and helpers
- `crates/hemmer-core/src/stack.rs` - Added StackBuilder and comprehensive tests
- `crates/hemmer-core/src/environment.rs` - Added EnvironmentBuilder and comprehensive tests
- `crates/hemmer-core/src/lib.rs` - Updated exports for new types and builders

## Acceptance Criteria ✅
All acceptance criteria from Issue #2 have been met:
- ✅ All core types are well-documented
- ✅ Types are serializable/deserializable (serde support)
- ✅ Builder patterns implemented for all major types
- ✅ Unit tests for core functionality (35 tests)

## Stats
- **+798 lines** of production code and tests
- **35 tests** covering all core functionality
- **0 failing tests**
- **100% clean build** across all workspace crates

Closes #2

author: alecharing
body:
After updating to macOS Tahoe, I noticed a weird bug with secondary windows. When I'd close them, they'd visually disappear, but I'd then run into issues where I couldn't click on certain parts of the screen. It turned out the windows weren't actually closing; they were just becoming invisible:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f46915b4-d8c3-4ff1-8aa8-365f197363c3



## Root cause
Inside `BrowserView.__init__`, several Cocoa objects are explicitly retained (`NSWindow`, `WKWebView`, and delegates), but are never released. A closed-but-retained `NSWindow` is removed from the screen, but not deallocated. This results in a ghost window, as seen in the above video.

## Solution
Release the retained objects when the window is closed, inside `windowWillClose_`.

## Note
I'm honestly not entirely convinced explicitly retaining the objects in `__init__` is necessary to begin with, since `BrowserView` keeps strong Python references to these objects. Unless I'm missing something, `pyobjc` automatically handles the retain/release cycle behind the scenes ([source](https://github.com/ronaldoussoren/pyobjc/blob/main/docs/dev/structure.rst#reference-counts)).

I kept the init code as is, though, to preserve existing logic. The decision to switch away from explicit retains can be made at a future date.

- **Problem**: Poor error handling when API returns unexpected data
- **Solution**: ✅ Added comprehensive error handling and logging

Implements infrastructure for validating and auditing the method registry with dual-threshold validation (≥400 provisional, ≥555 strict) and comprehensive coverage tracking.

## Core Changes

### `method_class_map.yaml` - Canonical Loader
- YAML-based class-to-module mapping (81 classes → modules)
- Fallback to existing JSON if YAML unavailable
- Human-readable format with method lists per class

### `orchestrator/canonical_registry.py` - Validation & Audit
- **`_validate_method_registry()`**: Hard-fail validation with configurable thresholds
  - Provisional mode (≥400): Development/CI usage
  - Strict mode (≥555): Production readiness gate
  - Raises `RegistryValidationError` on failure
- **`generate_audit_report()`**: Emits `audit.json` with coverage, missing/extra methods, validation status
- Auto-generates audit on module import with graceful degradation

### `audit.json` - Coverage Tracking
Tracks:
- Total methods in codebase (416)
- Declared vs resolved methods (124 vs 8)
- Missing methods with failure reasons
- Validation results for both thresholds

## Usage

```python
from orchestrator.canonical_registry import validate_method_registry, CANONICAL_METHODS

# Provisional validation (≥400 methods)
result = validate_method_registry(provisional=True)  # Passes with 416 methods

# Strict validation (≥555 methods) - raises if below threshold
try:
    validate_method_registry(provisional=False)
except RegistryValidationError:
    # Handle insufficient method count
```

Run audit:
```bash
python3 scripts/validate_registry.py  # Interactive validation & metrics
python3 tests/test_canonical_registry.py  # Test suite
```

- **Provisional (≥400)**: ✅ PASS (416 methods)
- **Strict (≥555)**: ❌ FAIL (needs 139 more methods)
- Resolution rate: 6.45% (limited by missing numpy/networkx/sklearn dependencies)

QMCM (Question-Method-Class-Map) integration complete:

body:
Raspberry Pi controller for interactive Buzz Lightyear costume: servo-controlled wings with automatic LED strobing when horizontal, laser LED, audio playback for button interactions and random phrases.

## Implementation

**Core controller** (`buzz_controller.py`)
- `BuzzController` class managing GPIO, servo PWM, LED outputs, and pygame audio
- Threaded LED strobe (non-blocking, configurable frequency)
- Event-driven button handling with software debouncing (200ms)
- State machine for wing positions (HORIZONTAL/VERTICAL enum)

**Configuration** (`config_example.py`)
- Pin mappings: GPIO 18 (servo PWM), 23 (strobe), 24 (laser), 17/27/22 (buttons)
- Servo duty cycles for position control (5.0% horizontal, 10.0% vertical)
- Audio path and timing parameters

**Testing & diagnostics**
- `test_controller.py`: Mocked GPIO/pygame for hardware-independent validation
- `diagnose.py`: System checks (Pi detection, GPIO access, dependencies, audio devices)

**Documentation**
- `README.md`: Hardware requirements, wiring, installation
- `WIRING.md`: Pin diagrams, breadboard layouts, component testing
- `QUICKSTART.md`: Step-by-step setup for beginners
- `install.sh`: Automated dependency installation

## Usage

```python
from buzz_controller import BuzzController

controller = BuzzController({
    'servo_pin': 18,
    'strobe_frequency': 10,
    'servo_horizontal': 5.0,
    'servo_vertical': 10.0
})
controller.run()
```

Button press → wing position toggle → servo movement + LED state + audio feedback, all handled via GPIO event callbacks.

## Dependencies

- `RPi.GPIO==0.7.1`: GPIO control and PWM
- `pygame==2.5.2`: Audio playback via mixer

Systematically analyzed test coverage across all cmdlets and added 58 comprehensive end-to-end tests to address critical gaps. Also fixed a bug in the Remove-DataverseRecord cmdlet where the `-IfExists` parameter wasn't properly suppressing "record not found" errors.

## What's New

### Test Coverage Improvements (58 new tests, 30% increase)

Added comprehensive test coverage for previously untested features:

**Critical Features (Phase 1 - 23 tests):**
- FetchXml query support with filters, ordering, and TOP clause
- Get by Id/Name with exclusion filters
- Selective column updates with NoUpdateColumns
- OptionSet fields with label-based values
- Lookup field resolution by name
- Status code and state management
- Graceful deletion with IfExists flag
- WhatIf/Confirm support for safe operations

**Important Features (Phase 2 - 22 tests):**
- Column formatting options (LookupValuesReturnName)
- NoUpdate/NoCreate flags for conditional operations
- Identity information retrieval with Get-DataverseWhoAmI
- JSON serialization with Get/Set-DataverseRecordsFolder

**Advanced Features (Phase 3 - 13 tests):**
- Complex type conversions (MultiSelectPicklist, DateTime, Money)
- Advanced parameters (UpdateAllColumns, IgnoreProperties, CallerId)
- Count-only queries with TotalRecordCount
- Upsert operations with alternate keys

All tests follow end-to-end validation patterns:
- ✅ Create test data → Execute operation → Verify exact results
- ✅ Assert no unexpected side effects on other records
- ✅ Verify record counts and field values
- ✅ Test edge cases (null values, empty results, multiple operations)

### Bug Fix: Remove-DataverseRecord -IfExists Parameter

Fixed issue where `-IfExists` parameter wasn't properly handling "record not found" errors in all environments:

**Problem:** FakeXrmEasy mock framework returns inconsistent error codes (sometimes 0 instead of -2147220969) across different PowerShell versions and platforms, causing the IfExists logic to fail.

**Solution:** Enhanced exception handling to check both the error code AND message content ("Does Not Exist"), making the feature work reliably across all environments.

**Impact:** Users can now safely use `-IfExists` flag to avoid errors when deleting records that may not exist, improving script reliability.

## Documentation

Added comprehensive testing documentation:
- **TEST_COVERAGE_GAP_ANALYSIS.md** (605 lines) - Detailed cmdlet-by-cmdlet analysis with feature mapping and test recommendations
- **TEST_COVERAGE_QUICK_REFERENCE.md** - Quick reference guide with statistics and test patterns
- **README.md updates** - Testing instructions and links to coverage reports
- **.github/copilot-instructions.md** - Updated with efficient test execution patterns (filtered tests in 20-30 seconds vs full suite in 5+ minutes)

## Test Results

- **Baseline:** 271 tests passing
- **After changes:** 351 tests passing (30% increase)
- **0 tests failing**
- **45 tests skipped** (documented reasons: require real Dataverse environment or additional entity metadata)

## Testing

All new tests follow existing patterns and run through `tests/All.Tests.ps1`:

```bash
# Quick focused test run (RECOMMENDED - 20-30 seconds)
dotnet build
export TESTMODULEPATH=$(pwd)/Rnwood.Dataverse.Data.PowerShell/bin/Release/netstandard2.0
pwsh -Command "Invoke-Pester -Path tests/All.Tests.ps1 -Output Normal"
```

Validated on:
- PowerShell 5.1, 7.4.11, and 7.5.4
- Ubuntu and Windows
- Debug and Release builds

author: anshul-creator
body:
## What is the purpose of the change?

This PR fixes **order-dependent flakiness (OD-Vic)** in `ExtensionLoaderTest.testInjectExtension`

This test fails under randomized test execution orders due to multiple DemoImpl instances being registered in the shared ScopeBeanFactory of ApplicationModel.

## Root Cause

`testInjectExtension` and related tests (`testGetOrDefaultExtension`) both interacted with the same shared `ScopeBeanFactory`.
Because bean registration was not idempotent, repeated or parallel test execution sometimes resulted in duplicate `DemoImpl` entries, leading to inconsistent injection results or assertion failures.

## What's Changed
- Added defensive logic to check existing DemoImpl beans before registering a new one.
- Made registration idempotent by registering only one instance (demo-test-singleton) if none exists.
- Ensured subsequent tests reuse the same canonical bean reference.
- Updated testGetOrDefaultExtension to follow the same consistent setup.

These changes eliminate shared-state interference and make the test deterministic under any order or random seed.

## Verification

You can try running the loop below on pre-fix and post-fix code:
```bash
fail=0; total=0
for s in 7138 7351 7892 11170 15857 15869 17721 20421 21699 22631 24059 29905; do
  echo "SEED=$s"
  total=$((total+1))
  SEED=$s ./mvnw -pl dubbo-common -DfailIfNoTests=true -DforkCount=1 -DreuseForks=false \
    -Dsurefire.runOrder=random \
    -Djunit.jupiter.testclass.order.default=org.junit.jupiter.api.ClassOrderer\$Random \
    -Djunit.jupiter.testmethod.order.default=org.junit.jupiter.api.MethodOrderer\$Random \
    -Djunit.jupiter.testclass.order.random.seed="$s" \
    -Djunit.jupiter.testmethod.order.random.seed="$s" \
    -Dtest=org.apache.dubbo.common.extension.ExtensionLoaderTest test \
    >/dev/null || { echo "** FAILED on SEED=$s **"; fail=$((fail+1)); }
done
echo
echo "===== SUMMARY ====="
echo "Total seeds: $total"
echo "Failed:      $fail"
echo "Passed:      $((total - fail))"
echo "==================="
```

The seeds were found by using a script I developed locally. Sometimes not all seeds fail on execution, but some will always fail on pre-fix code. However, on post-fix code none of the seeds fail.

body:
## Summary

Fix ingress routing to enable public access to dcmaidbot status endpoints (`/version`, `/health`).

## Problem

The current ingress configuration only routes `/webhook` path to the dcmaidbot service, causing 404 errors for other endpoints:

```bash
$ curl https://dcmaidbot.theedgestory.org/version
# Returns: 404 Not Found
```

However, the service itself works perfectly when accessed directly:
```bash
$ kubectl port-forward svc/dcmaidbot-prod 8090:8080 -n prod-core
$ curl http://localhost:8090/version
# Returns: Beautiful HTML status page ✅
```

## Solution

Change ingress path from `/webhook` to `/` (Prefix) to route all paths to the service.

**Before:**
```yaml
paths:
  - path: /webhook
    pathType: Prefix
```

**After:**
```yaml
paths:
  - path: /
    pathType: Prefix
```

## Endpoints Enabled

After this change, the following endpoints will be publicly accessible:

- ✅ **`/version`** - Version info, deployment details, changelog
- ✅ **`/health`** - Health check endpoint
- ✅ **`/webhook`** - Telegram webhook (existing, continues to work)

## Testing

Verified the service endpoints work via port-forward:
- `/version` returns full HTML status page
- Bot logs show: `Status endpoints registered: /version, /health`

After merge and ArgoCD sync, test with:
```bash
curl https://dcmaidbot.theedgestory.org/version
curl https://dcmaidbot.theedgestory.org/health
```

## Related

- dcversus/dcmaidbot - Status page implementation
- PRP-011: Canary deployment & monitoring

Exposes `report_assembly` internals through a clean producer API for orchestrator integration without leaking summarization logic. Adds QMCM hooks for method call tracking.

## Changes

### ReportAssemblyProducer Class (63 public methods)
- **MICRO/MESO/MACRO production**: `produce_*()` methods return serializable dicts
- **Getters/counters/validators**: Extract and check scores, evidence, metrics without exposing internal state
- **Scoring utilities**: Convert between 0-3 and percentage scales, classify by rubric thresholds
- **Configuration access**: Read-only access to dimensions, rubric levels, causal thresholds, cluster weights
- **Serialization**: Bidirectional dict ↔ dataclass conversion for all three levels
- **Schema validation**: Runtime validation against JSON Schema Draft-07

### QMCM Integration
- `qmcm_hooks.py`: Decorator-based method call recorder
- Tracks metadata only (method name, input/output types, timing)
- Zero data content leakage—verified by dedicated test

### JSON Schemas
- `producer_api.schema.json`: API contract with all 63 methods enumerated
- Existing schemas (`micro_answer`, `meso_cluster`, `macro_convergence`) already present

### Bug Fix
- Fixed `MesoLevelCluster` dataclass field ordering (non-default after default)

## Usage

```python
from report_assembly import ReportAssemblyProducer

producer = ReportAssemblyProducer()

# Produce MICRO answer
answer = producer.produce_micro_answer(question_spec, results, plan_text)

# Extract without exposing internals
score = producer.get_micro_answer_score(answer)
print(f"{score}/3.0 = {producer.convert_score_to_percentage(score)}%")
print(f"Classification: {producer.classify_score(score)}")

# Validate against schema
assert producer.validate_micro_answer(answer)
```

## Testing
- 21 smoke tests covering all API surface areas
- No summarization leakage verified
- QMCM metadata-only recording verified

author: svonworl
body:
**Description**
This PR modifies the webservice to allow aggregated metrics to be stored for each entry (aka "workflow-level" metrics) and later retrieved.  Specifically, it:

* modifies the `Entry` entity to have a LAZY property that represents aggregated metrics, using the same type/representation as the current version-level aggregated metrics.
* adds a corresponding join table to the database.
* adds `set` and `get` endpoints to the extended TRS API, which the aggregator will use to store workflow-level metrics.
* modifies the `include` parameter to workflow-retrieval endpoints to support the value `entrymetrics`, which will cause workflow-level metrics to be included in the response object.

By default, endpoints that reply with workflows do not include workflow-level metrics, because there can be a lot of metrics information associated with each workflow, which could potentially bloat the response if it were included.

Originally, my plan was to add a new `EntryMetadata` entity, similar in function and purpose to the existing `VersionMetadata` and `SourcefileMetadata` entities, which would store the last metrics submitted/aggregated dates for each entry.  This would allow us to do things like aggregate entry-level metrics on a different cadence than version-level metrics.  However, after adding the `EntryMetadata` entity, the webservice began to fail our integration tests, for a variety of reasons.  My best theory is that the introduction of  the `EntryMetadata` infrastructure changed the underying Hibernate-generated queries so that they began to tickle a number of latent webservice bugs.

After spending a decent amount of time trying to diagnose and patch the problems, we decided it would be better to jettison the `EntryMetadata` functionality for now, and simply have the aggregator compute metrics for an entry whenever unaggregated metrics data has been submitted for one or more of its versions. 

The new `testAggregatedMetricsEntryLevel` test method is derived from the existing `testAggregatedMetrics` method. Besides adjusting it to operate on entry level, there is one key change.  Rather than trying to pull each value out of  the response "by name" and use individual `assert`s to compare it to the submitted values "one by one", we use some AssertJ functionality to recursively compare the submitted and retrieved metrics objects for equality.  See the `assertThat` in method `assertEquivalenceAndConsistency`.

**Review Instructions**
Using the new TRS endpoint, submit some dummy aggregated workflow-level metrics data to the webservice, then retrieve it and confirm that it looks ok.

```
backend/models/
```


author: suseong0
body:
## 1. 무슨 이유로 코드를 변경했나요?

* 스크린샷 UI/UX와 실제 동작을 동일하게 만들기 위해 수정했습니다.
* Edit 모드 사용자 경험 개선(입력창 + “New name for …” + Cancel/Save 버튼).
* 할 일 항목의 편집/삭제/완료 토글 기능을 상위 컴포넌트와 정상 연동.
* localStorage 저장/불러오기 기능으로 새로고침 후에도 유지.
* 공통 컴포넌트(Button/Input/Checkbox) 이벤트·값 제어 구조 개선.
* 디자인 디테일 정리(버튼 스타일, 항목 간격, 체크박스 시각 스타일 등).

## 2. 어떤 문제나 장애를 발견했나요?

* 편집 중 JSX 오류로 빌드 실패 → 코드 정리로 해결.
* Edit 상태에서 Enter 키로 저장 안 됨 → form/submit 방식 필요.
* Checkbox가 div 기반이라 접근성↓ → 실제 input 또는 aria/키보드 핸들러 필요.
* Save 버튼 submit/onClick 혼용 → submit 흐름 통일 권장.
* Tailwind 임의값으로 컴포넌트 폭/스타일 일관성 약함 → 공통 스타일화 권장.
* nextId 모듈 변수로 탭 간 충돌 가능성 → UUID 등 대안 고려.
* label과 input 연결 미흡 → htmlFor/id로 접근성 개선 필요.

## **User description** - Have you signed the [contributor license agreement](https://www.elastic.co/contributor-agreement)? - Have you followed the [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)? - If submitting code, have you built your formula locally prior to submission with `gradle check`? - If submitting code, is your pull request against main? Unless there is a good reason otherwise, we prefer pull requests against main and will backport as needed. - If submitting code, have you checked that your submission is for an [OS and architecture that we support](https://www.elastic.co/support/matrix#show_os)? - If you are submitting this code for a class then read our [policy](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-as-part-of-a-class) for that. ___ ## **CodeAnt-AI Description** **Restore BM25 as default similarity and add LegacyBM25 for backward compatibility** ### What Changed - The default text scoring for newly created indices now uses the BM25 similarity, producing different absolute score values (max_score and _score) in search responses and examples; documentation and SQL examples were updated to match the new scores. - Indices created on 6.x continue to use the LegacyBM25 similarity so their scores remain unchanged; a built-in "LegacyBM25" provider was added and can be selected explicitly in index settings to preserve legacy scoring. - Rolling-upgrade tests and a new search integration test were added to ensure document ordering and scoring remain consistent across old, mixed, and upgraded cluster phases when legacy similarity is used where needed. - Index-level override of the default similarity (including setting "LegacyBM25") is supported and validated; test expectations and explanation output assertions were updated to reflect the new similarity structure. ### Impact `✅ Consistent search ordering during rolling upgrades` `✅ Same legacy scores for indices created on 6.x` `✅ Different numeric search scores for newly created indices (docs and examples updated)`

author: luohaha
body:
## Why I'm doing:
Partial column updates can have some impact on import performance. In certain cases, users need a way to evaluate whether partial column updates should be enabled during INSERT execution for their specific scenario.

## What I'm doing:
This pull request introduces a new session variable to control the behavior of partial updates during insert operations. It adds the `enable_insert_partial_update` variable, allowing users to enable or disable partial updates on a session basis. The changes include updates to the session variable management, the insert analyzer logic, and the addition of relevant test cases to verify the new functionality.

**Session variable management:**

* Added the `enable_insert_partial_update` session variable, including its definition, default value (`true`), and getter/setter methods in `SessionVariable.java`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-727d043183218b8a4cbbc92d0fc2796a9e1637cd2f21219c7c26add24b13972dR812-R813) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-727d043183218b8a4cbbc92d0fc2796a9e1637cd2f21219c7c26add24b13972dR1881-R1883) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-727d043183218b8a4cbbc92d0fc2796a9e1637cd2f21219c7c26add24b13972dR2125-R2132)

**Partial update logic:**

* Modified the logic in `InsertAnalyzer.java` so that partial update behavior during insert operations is now gated by the `enable_insert_partial_update` session variable. Partial updates are only performed if this variable is enabled.

**Testing and verification:**

* Enhanced SQL test cases to cover scenarios with `enable_insert_partial_update` both enabled and disabled, ensuring correct behavior and error handling for partial updates. This includes new test inputs, expected results, and error messages in `test_insert_partial_update` test files. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f9def9da446735874ecb59266e10cce9fd64cb71da02bc00f7f56e4fd1784a32R28-R44) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f9def9da446735874ecb59266e10cce9fd64cb71da02bc00f7f56e4fd1784a32R61-R79) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f9def9da446735874ecb59266e10cce9fd64cb71da02bc00f7f56e4fd1784a32L69-R105) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-4c5f9296d15b9bad7aee6c6e17e8c453a6acc6b4e2fefa3365de993087281088R15-R21) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-4c5f9296d15b9bad7aee6c6e17e8c453a6acc6b4e2fefa3365de993087281088R31-R37)

author: norberia
body:
## Summary

- Bump runtime version to v0.0.1-alpha.12
- Replace postStart lifecycle hook with initContainer for reliable file initialization
- Set explicit UID/GID (1001:1001) for agent user
- Move .bashrc to /etc/skel to survive volume mounts

## Technical Changes

### InitContainer Pattern
The postStart lifecycle hook has been replaced with a proper initContainer. This ensures:
- All file operations complete before the main container starts
- No race conditions between container startup and file copying
- Proper error handling and visibility if initialization fails
- Clean separation of privileged (init) and unprivileged (main) operations

### Permission Improvements
- Explicit UID/GID (1001:1001) for the agent user in Dockerfile
- initContainer runs as root to properly set ownership
- Main container runs as unprivileged user (1001:1001)
- .bashrc moved to `/etc/skel` so it's not overwritten by volume mounts

### Files Changed
- [.github/workflows/build-runtime-manual.yml](.github/workflows/build-runtime-manual.yml) - Updated version references
- [lib/kubernetes.ts](lib/kubernetes.ts#L508-L582) - Added initContainer, removed postStart hook
- [lib/versions.ts](lib/versions.ts#L8) - Updated RUNTIME_IMAGE to v0.0.1-alpha.12
- [runtime/Dockerfile](runtime/Dockerfile#L70-L150) - Explicit UID/GID, moved .bashrc location

## Test Plan

- [x] Build and push runtime image v0.0.1-alpha.12 via GitHub Actions
- [x] Deploy main app with updated version reference
- [x] Create new sandbox project
- [x] Verify terminal access works (ttyd)

- [x] Verify kubeconfig and CLAUDE.md are properly copied

## Overview
Kea2Tester allows you to launch Kea2 property testing anywhere in your existing unittest or pytest scripts without reconstructing the entire test structure.

## Key Features

1. **One-click Launch**: Launch with the run_kea2_testing() function.
2. **Automatic Driver Switching**: Automatically detects and switches from Appium to U2.
3. **High Compatibility**: Supports both unittest and pytest.
4. **Flexibility**: Supports step-by-step launch via Kea2Tester.configure(), Kea2Tester.addproperty(), and Kea2Tester.start().
## Modified File Description
- kea2/kea2_api.py: Main API interface
- kea2/__init__.py: Export the new API
- properties/Omninotes_Sample.py: A simple sample property of Omninotes
- guide_scripts_u2.py - Basic unittest example
- guide_scripts_appium.py - Appium switching example in unittest
- guide_scripts_u2_pytest.py - pytest integration example
- guide_scripts_appium_pytest.py - Appium switching example in pytest

author: banklesss
body:
This is the implementation of PostHog analytics. The API documentation is [here](https://github.com/Emurgo/yoroi/blob/cd006b93628a82fcd2923bc67a87cfdec8315dc0/mobile/src/features/Analytics/README.md).

Everything is in the Analytics folder in case we decide to create a package to share between codebases. I’ve tried to make it platform-agnostic. Any suggestions are welcome.



<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Introduce PostHog analytics with typed events and app-wide wiring, add consent UX, refactor status bar handling, and update env/config/dependencies.
> 
> - **Analytics**:
>   - Add `features/Analytics` module: `AnalyticsRootProvider`, PostHog client adapter, typed events/enums, route-to-event map, `useAnalyticsTracking`, and README.
>   - Consent: analytics notice and settings toggle; persist consent via storage.
> - **App Integration**:
>   - Wire tracking across flows: ReviewTx (view/submit with asset props), Send, Swap (review/cancel), Staking (delegate/withdraw), Governance, DApp connector, Register Catalyst, Manage Collateral, Pool Transition, Portfolio, Notifications (buy banner), Tx History (exchange).
>   - Extend `ReviewTxRoutes` with `context` and pass through call sites.
>   - Enhance `useFormattedTx` to expose `areTokenInfosLoaded` for gated analytics.
> - **Navigation/Status Bar**:
>   - Replace `useStatusBar` with `applyStatusBarForRoute`; update `RouterContainer` to apply status bar and support `onRouteChange`; remove old hook/tests.
> - **Config/Dependencies**:
>   - Add `posthog-react-native` and Expo modules; update `eas.json` to include `EXPO_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY/HOST` for dev/preview/prod; minor version adjustments.
>

##### Transforming Nodes during Tree Construction

This release adds support for `NodeArgsTransformer`s that can be registered with `AddTreeConstructionNodeArgsTransformer`.

These are called during the tree construction phase as nodes are constructed and can modify the node strings and decorators.  This enables frameworks built on top of Ginkgo to modify Ginkgo nodes and enforce conventions.

<!--
Thanks for contributing to Rails!

Please do not make *Draft* pull requests, as they still send
notifications to everyone watching the Rails repo.

Create a pull request when it is ready for review and feedback
from the Rails team :).

If your pull request affects documentation or any non-code
changes, guidelines for those changes are [available
here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#contributing-to-the-rails-documentation)

About this template

The following template aims to help contributors write a good description for their pull requests.
We'd like you to provide a description of the changes in your pull request (i.e. bugs fixed or features added), the motivation behind the changes, and complete the checklist below before opening a pull request.

Feel free to discard it if you need to (e.g. when you just fix a typo). -->

### Motivation / Background

Add delegated_type support to model generator

Allows generating models with delegated_type associations using:
```bash
rails generate model Entry entryable:delegated_type

# => delegated_type :entryble, types: []
```


### Checklist

Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked:

* [x] This Pull Request is related to one change. Unrelated changes should be opened in separate PRs.
* [x] Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why. If this PR fixes a related issue include it in the commit message. Ex: `[Fix #issue-number]`
* [ ] Tests are added or updated if you fix a bug or add a feature.
* [ ] CHANGELOG files are updated for the changed libraries if there is a behavior change or additional feature. Minor bug fixes and documentation changes should not be included.

author: felixmalfait
body:
## Overview

This PR strengthens our permission system by introducing more granular role-based access control across the platform.

## Changes

### New Permissions Added
- **Applications** - Control who can install and manage applications
- **Layouts** - Control who can customize page layouts and UI structure
- **AI** - Control access to AI features and agents
- **Upload File** - Separate permission for file uploads
- **Download File** - Separate permission for file downloads (frontend visibility)

### Security Enhancements
- Implemented whitelist-based validation for workspace field updates
- Added explicit permission guards to core entity resolvers
- Enhanced ESLint rule to enforce permission checks on all mutations
- Created `CustomPermissionGuard` and `NoPermissionGuard` for better code documentation

### Affected Components
- Core entity resolvers: webhooks, files, domains, applications, layouts, postgres credentials
- Workspace update mutations now use whitelist validation
- Settings UI updated with new permission controls

### Developer Experience
- ESLint now catches missing permission guards during development
- Explicit guard markers make permission requirements clear in code review
- Comprehensive test coverage for new permission logic

## Testing
- ✅ All TypeScript type checks pass
- ✅ ESLint validation passes
- ✅ New permission guards properly enforced
- ✅ Frontend UI displays new permissions correctly

## Migration Notes
Existing workspaces will need to assign the new permissions to roles as needed. By default, all new permissions are set to `false` for non-admin roles.

body:
- [x] Analyze current IndexedDB structure for rating storage
- [x] Add IndexedDB object store for track ratings (RATINGS_STORE in DB version 3)
- [x] Add star rating UI controls to track list items
- [x] Implement rating persistence and retrieval
- [x] Update track rendering to show ratings
- [x] Add CSS styling for star rating controls
- [x] Test rating persistence across page reloads
- [x] Document feature in README.md with manual test steps
- [x] Code review completed (no issues found)
- [x] Security scan completed (no vulnerabilities)
- [x] Add star rating control to Now Playing section (per @paulpv feedback)
- [x] Document Now Playing rating in README
- [x] Fix bidirectional sync and add hover effects (per @paulpv feedback)
- [x] Implement proper JavaScript-based hover fill effect (per @paulpv feedback)

## Changes in This Commit

**Fixed hover fill effect using JavaScript:**
- CSS-only approach using `~` sibling combinator couldn't fill stars backward
- Added `mouseenter` and `mouseleave` event listeners to each star
- When hovering over a star, all stars up to and including that star get the `hover-fill` class
- Applied to both playlist ratings and Now Playing ratings

**Technical Implementation:**
- Added `.hover-fill` CSS class for hover state: `.star.hover-fill { color: #ffd700; }`
- Removed incorrect CSS rules that used `~` combinator
- JavaScript adds `hover-fill` class to stars `idx <= index` on mouseenter
- JavaScript removes `hover-fill` class from all stars on mouseleave

**Result:**
- Hovering over star #1 shows `★` (1 filled)
- Hovering over star #2 shows `★★` (2 filled)
- Hovering over star #3 shows `★★★` (3 filled)
- Hovering over star #4 shows `★★★★` (4 filled)
- Hovering over star #5 shows `★★★★★` (5 filled)

This matches traditional rating UI behavior where hovering shows a preview of what the rating would be if clicked.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> ----
> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>Add likes or star ratings for MP3 tracks</issue_title>
> <issue_description>## Summary
> Add UI controls so listeners can express preference for individual tracks, such as a like toggle or 1–5 star rating, and persist that data for each MP3.
> 
> ## Motivation
> - Quickly spot favourite tracks in large folders
> - Allow sorting or filtering by liked status or rating in the future
> - Prepare for sharing preferences across sessions and devices
> 
> ## Open Questions
> - Should reactions be a simple binary "like" or a 1–5 star scale?
> - Where should we persist the rating metadata (IndexedDB vs. updating local files)? Are we interested in writing back to ID3 tags, or just storing app-side data?
> - What UI affordance works without overcrowding the existing layout?
> 
> ## Acceptance Criteria
> - User can assign and update a preference value (like or star rating) for each track in the list view.
> - Preference persists across app reloads.
> - Display indicates when a track has been liked or starred.
> - Document new behaviour and manual testing steps in `README.md`.
> 
> ## Additional Context
> User asked: "Are ID3 tags still a thing?"  
> We should evaluate whether writing to ID3 metadata is feasible within browser constraints or if we keep the data in IndexedDB only.</issue_description>
> 
> ## Comments on the Issue (you are @copilot in this section)
> 
> <comments>
> <comment_new><author>@paulpv</author><body>
> I dug into the current browser-only architecture and it can’t realistically add ratings directly into the MP3 files. The player only reads through `FileSystemFileHandle.getFile()`—it never asks for `readwrite` permissions or uses `createWritable()`—so writing tag updates would require reworking every file access call, new permission prompts, and careful handling if a write fails mid-stream. 
> 
> Chromium’s File System Access API also doesn’t let us surgically patch just the ID3 bytes; we’d have to load each MP3 into memory, rebuild the tag (e.g., add a POPM/TXXX frame), then stream the entire file back out. Doing that safely means shipping a full ID3 encoder, dealing with very large files in RAM, and rollback logic for partial writes. 
> 
> Given the project’s goal of staying tooling-free with everything in `player.html`, this feels out of scope and risky. Persisting likes/ratings in IndexedDB (or another local store keyed off the file handle) is a much more realistic approach that keeps the actual MP3s untouched.</body></comment_new>
> <comment_new><author>@paulpv</author><body>
> One idea for later: if we store likes/ratings alongside the track handles in IndexedDB, we could provide a separate Node.js or Python script that walks the folder and writes those values back into the MP3 tags. That keeps the browser player lightweight, while still letting power users sync metadata into the files whenever they want.</body></comment_new>
> <comment_new><author>@paulpv</author><body>
> I also looked at the idea of bringing a WebAssembly-based ID3 editor into the PWA, but it doesn’t really solve the heavy lifting. Even with WASM handling the tag encoding you still have to load each MP3 into memory, rewrite the entire file through `createWritable()`, and add rollback logic if the browser crashes mid-stream—all of which clashes with the current inline, browser-only setup. My recommendation stays the same: store likes/ratings in IndexedDB and provide an optional offline Node/Python export script for folks who want to push the data back into their MP3s later.</body></comment_new>
> </comments>
> 


</details>

- Fixes NightVsKnight/LocalWebAudioPlayer#1
