author: copilot
body:
Refactored UOM handling to centralize management in Organization plugin with base unit normalization. All inventory quantities now stored in base units with runtime conversion for display, following `docs/uom-normalization-guide.md`.

## Database Schema

**Procurement**: Added `base_uom_id`, `purchase_uom_id` to `purchaseable_items`
- `base_uom_id`: Normalization reference (nullable)
- `purchase_uom_id`: Display preference (nullable)

**Inventory**: Added base UOM tracking to `warehouse_items` and audit trail to `inventory_ledgers`
- `warehouse_items.base_uom_id`: Defines unit for `quantity_on_hand` (always base)
- `inventory_ledgers.original_transaction_uom_id`: Preserves actual transaction UOM
- `inventory_ledgers.original_transaction_quantity`: Audit trail

All foreign keys reference `omsb_organization_unit_of_measures`.

## Model Changes

Updated models with UOM relationships, validation, and dropdown methods:
- `PurchaseableItem`: Base/purchase UOM with `getBaseUomIdOptions()`, `getPurchaseUomIdOptions()`
- `WarehouseItem`: Base/display UOM with quantity normalization
- `InventoryLedger`: Base UOM + transaction audit trail

## Usage Pattern

```php
use Omsb\Organization\Services\UOMNormalizationService;

// Normalize transaction to base UOM
$service = new UOMNormalizationService();
$normalized = $service->normalize(2, $boxUom); // 2 BOX → 144 ROLL

// Store in base, preserve original
InventoryLedger::createEntry([
    'base_uom_id' => $rollUom->id,
    'quantity_change' => $normalized['base_quantity'], // 144
    'original_transaction_uom_id' => $boxUom->id,      // BOX
    'original_transaction_quantity' => 2,               // 2
    // ...
]);

// Display conversion at runtime
$displayQty = $service->denormalize($item->quantity_on_hand, $rollUom, $boxUom);
```

## Test Coverage

59 test cases across 4 suites:
- `UOMNormalizationServiceTest`: Normalization, conversion, multi-UOM, compatibility
- `PurchaseableItemTest`: UOM fields, validation, relationships
- `WarehouseItemTest`: Base UOM constraints, quantity management
- `InventoryLedgerTest`: Audit trail, immutability, cost calculation

## Documentation

- `UOM_IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md`: Architecture overview and migration guide
- `CONTROLLER_VIEW_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md`: Controller/view integration examples with code snippets

## Notes

Controller and view integration requires domain knowledge. Integration guide provides complete examples for:
- PO line item normalization
- Goods receipt with flexible UOM entry
- Multi-UOM physical counts
- Form configurations and partials

This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [com.unboundid:unboundid-ldapsdk](https://redirect.github.com/pingidentity/ldapsdk) | compile | patch | `4.0.5` -> `4.0.14` |

---

> [!WARNING]
> Some dependencies could not be looked up. Check the warning logs for more information.

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>pingidentity/ldapsdk (com.unboundid:unboundid-ldapsdk)</summary>

### [`v4.0.14`](https://redirect.github.com/pingidentity/ldapsdk/releases/tag/4.0.14): UnboundID LDAP SDK for Java 4.0.14

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pingidentity/ldapsdk/compare/4.0.13...4.0.14)

We have just released version 4.0.14 of the [UnboundID LDAP SDK for Java](https://redirect.github.com/pingidentity/ldapsdk). It is available for download from the releases page of our GitHub repository (<https://github.com/pingidentity/ldapsdk/releases>), from the Files page of our SourceForge repository (<https://sourceforge.net/projects/ldap-sdk/files/>), and from the Maven Central Repository (<https://search.maven.org/search?q=g:com.unboundid%20AND%20a:unboundid-ldapsdk&core=gav>).

The LDAP SDK release notes are available at <https://docs.ldap.com/ldap-sdk/docs/release-notes.html>, but the changes included in this release are as follows:

- Fixed an issue in which LDAP URLs with consecutive percent-encoded bytes were not decoded correctly.

- Fixed an issue that could cause the LDAP SDK to incorrectly handle data read from a server when the communication was protected with SASL integrity or confidentiality. Thanks to Boris Danilovich for reporting the problem and identifying the cause.

- Fixed an issue that prevented the `searchrate` tool from running if neither a base DN pattern nor an LDAP URL pattern was provided.

- Improved the logic that the LDAP SDK used when selecting the cipher suites to use when establishing a TLS-secured connection. Weaker suites are disabled, and the enabled suites are prioritized so that those offering forward secrecy and stronger encryption are preferred.

- Added a new `FullLDAPInterface` that extends `LDAPInterface` and adds support for `close`, `bind`, and `processExtendedOperation` methods. The existing `LDAPConnection`, `AbstractConnectionPool`, and `InMemoryDirectoryServer` classes have been updated to implement this interface.

- Added a new non-final `MockableLDAPConnection` class that makes it easier to mock an `LDAPConnection` instance. It implements `FullLDAPInterface` and wraps a provided `LDAPConnection`. If you create a `MockableLDAPConnection` subclass, then you may override any of the `FullLDAPInterface` methods to provide whatever logic you desire for them. Any non-overridden methods will invoke the corresponding method on the provided `LDAPConnection` instance.

- Fixed a minor typo in the `ldapsearch` usage information

### [`v4.0.13`](https://redirect.github.com/pingidentity/ldapsdk/releases/tag/4.0.13): UnboundID LDAP SDK for Java 4.0.13

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pingidentity/ldapsdk/compare/4.0.12...4.0.13)

We have just released version 4.0.13 of the [UnboundID LDAP SDK for Java](https://redirect.github.com/pingidentity/ldapsdk). It is available for download from the releases page of our GitHub repository (<https://github.com/pingidentity/ldapsdk/releases>), from the Files page of our SourceForge repository (<https://sourceforge.net/projects/ldap-sdk/files/>), and from the Maven Central Repository (<https://search.maven.org/search?q=g:com.unboundid%20AND%20a:unboundid-ldapsdk&core=gav>).

This is a minor update that is primarily intended to serve the upcoming Ping Identity Directory Server 8.0.0.0 release. The LDAP SDK release notes are available online at <https://docs.ldap.com/ldap-sdk/docs/release-notes.html>, but the changes included in this release are as follows:

- Added support for debugging connection pool interactions, including checking out and releasing connections, as well as establishing and closing connections for use in the pool.

- Fixed an issue in the prompt trust manager that could cause it to incorrectly display a warning for some certificates with a basic constraints extension that included the optional path length constraint.

- Updated the `manage-certificates check-certificate-usability` command to add an additional check to see whether the certificate at the root of the chain is found in the JVM’s default set of trusted issuer certificates. If it is not found, the tool will display a notice, but it will still complete with a success result.

- Fixed an issue in `manage-certificates` that could prevent it from correctly showing the key agreement usage when displaying verbose information about a certificate with the key usage extension.

- Fixed an issue that could prevent properly decoding an authority key identifier extension that included the optional authorityCertIssuer element in an X.509 certificate.

- Made the `ManageCertificates.readCertificatesFromFile` method public so that it can be used outside of the LDAP SDK. This method can be used to read a set of PEM-encoded or DER-encoded X.509 certificates from a specified file.

- Made the `ManageCertificates.readCertificateSigningRequestFromFile` method so that it can be used outside of the LDAP SDK. This method can be used to read a PEM-encoded or DER-encoded PKCS [#​10](https://redirect.github.com/pingidentity/ldapsdk/issues/10) certificate signing request from a file.

- Updated the passphrase-encrypted output stream to provide an option to override the default key factory iteration count.

- Updated support for the exec task to add an option to specify the path to use as the current working directory when invoking the specified command. Previously, the server would always use the server instance root directory, and that will still be the default if no alternate working directory is specified.

- Added an additional `StaticUtils.getEnvironmentVariable` method variant that can be used to provide a default value that should be used if the specified environment variable is not set.

- Added an additional `StaticUtils.getStackTrace` method variant that allows you to limit the number of stack frames to include from code before the call into the LDAP SDK. Also, updated `StaticUtils.getExceptionMessage` when invoked for a `NullPointerException` so that it now shows all frames from the LDAP SDK (and anything that the LDAP SDK calls), and up to three frames from the code before the call into the LDAP SDK.

### [`v4.0.12`](https://redirect.github.com/pingidentity/ldapsdk/releases/tag/4.0.12): UnboundID LDAP SDK for Java 4.0.12

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pingidentity/ldapsdk/compare/4.0.11...4.0.12)

We have just released version 4.0.12 of the [UnboundID LDAP SDK for Java](https://redirect.github.com/pingidentity/ldapsdk). It is available for download from the releases page of our GitHub repository (<https://github.com/pingidentity/ldapsdk/releases>), from the Files page of our SourceForge repository (<https://sourceforge.net/projects/ldap-sdk/files/>), and from the Maven Central Repository (<https://search.maven.org/search?q=g:com.unboundid%20AND%20a:unboundid-ldapsdk&core=gav>).

The LDAP SDK release notes are available at <https://docs.ldap.com/ldap-sdk/docs/release-notes.html>, but the changes included in this release are as follows:

- Fixed an issue in the write timeout handler that could prevent it from properly cleaning up a timer task object for a connection if an attempt to establish that connection failed. This regression, which was introduced in the 4.0.11 release, could lead to a gradual increase in memory consumption over time.

- Updated the write timeout handler so that it will now shut down its background thread after all LDAP connections have been closed.

- Fixed an issue with the JVM-default trust manager that could cause it to incorrectly abort TLS negotiation if the server presented only a partial certificate

body:
Create browser-based Pixelsort implementation for mobile devices. No crop functionality per requirements.

## Implementation

**Core Engine (`web/pixelsorter.js`)**
- Ported all 3 sorting algorithms from Rust: Horizontal, Vertical, Diagonal
- Brightness-based interval detection with threshold support
- HSV color space operations for hue shifting
- 3 sort modes: Brightness, Black, White

**Application (`web/app.js`)**
- Camera capture via MediaDevices API with environment-facing preference
- File upload with immediate processing
- Real-time pixel sorting on parameter changes
- Save & iterate workflow with auto-incrementing filenames
- Session management

**UI (`web/styles.css`, `web/index.html`)**
- Touch-optimized controls: 80-240px circular buttons
- Large slider handles (50px) with visible value displays
- Two-phase flow: Input → Edit (no crop phase)
- Responsive grid layout with landscape mode support
- 2s splash screen with fade animation
- PWA manifest for mobile installation

## Algorithm Parity

JavaScript implementation matches Rust sorting logic:

```javascript
// Find intervals based on brightness threshold
const intervals = this.findIntervals(rowPixels, threshold);

// Sort each segment by mode (Brightness/Black/White)
for (const [start, end] of intervals) {
    const segment = rowPixels.slice(start, end);
    segment.sort((a, b) => this.sortKey(a, sortMode) - this.sortKey(b, sortMode));
}
```

## Screenshots

**Input Phase**
![Input](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/938afc8c-af82-44ef-84a6-6981b3cba709)

**Horizontal Sorting with Threshold**

**Hue Shift Applied**
![Hue](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73b451e1-ba99-41bc-82d3-ea67c1f4a1bc)

## Deployment

Static files only. Works on any HTTP server or hosting platform (GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel). HTTPS required for camera access on non-localhost domains.

## Summary
Fixes #33 

The import command previously saved all imported secrets in plaintext by setting both the `value` and `default` fields. This created a security risk where secrets could be accidentally committed to version control.

This PR makes the `--provider` flag required for the import command, ensuring that imported secrets are always encrypted using a specified provider.

## Changes
- Made `--provider` flag required for import command
- Added provider validation and capability checks
- Import now encrypts values using the specified provider
- Removed automatic plaintext storage in `default` field
- Added helpful error messages for unsupported provider types

## Example Usage

**Before (unsafe - stores plaintext):**
```bash
fnox import < .env  # Would store secrets in plaintext
```

**After (secure - requires encryption):**
```bash
fnox import --provider age < .env  # Encrypts secrets with age provider
```

## Test Plan
- [x] Built the project successfully
- [x] Verified `--provider` flag is now required
- [x] Confirmed import command fails with helpful error when provider flag is missing
- [x] Code passes pre-commit hooks (cargo-fmt, cargo-check)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Implements a prioritized if_missing setting (CLI/env/secret/top-level/default) used across commands, documents it, adds tests, and requires an encryption provider for imports.
> 
> - **Core/Resolver**:
>   - Add centralized `resolve_if_missing_behavior` and `handle_provider_error` with full priority chain (CLI/env → secret → top-level → base env default → warn).
>   - Update `resolve_secret` to use new missing-secret handling.
> - **CLI/Settings/Config**:
>   - Add global `--if-missing` flag; plumb through `settings::CliSnapshot` and generated settings.
>   - Support env vars `FNOX_IF_MISSING` and `FNOX_IF_MISSING_DEFAULT`.
>   - Add top-level `Config.if_missing` and merge logic.
> - **Commands**:
>   - Update `exec`, `export`, and `ci_redact` to use centralized missing-secret resolution and error handling.
> - **Import**:
>   - Require `--provider`; validate provider and capabilities; encrypt values for encryption providers; disallow remote-storage imports; improved messages.
> - **Docs**:
>   - README: new “Handling Missing Secrets” section with modes, priority, and examples; list new env vars.
>   - Settings registry: add `if_missing` and `if_missing_default` entries.
> - **Tests**:
>   - Add `test/if_missing_priority.bats` covering precedence and runtime overrides.
>

author: yarivhashaicomet
body:
## Details

Fixed Qwen VL models not being recognized as vision-capable in the Playground, causing the Run button to be disabled when using images.

### Root Cause

The `model_prices_and_context_window.json` is synced daily from [LiteLLM](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/refs/heads/main/model_prices_and_context_window.json). It uses `openrouter/qwen/qwen-vl-plus` naming, but the UI uses `qwen/qwen-vl-plus`. The `supportsImageInput` function couldn't match these different formats.

### Solution

Added a pattern-based override in `modelCapabilities.ts` that checks hardcoded regex patterns before the JSON config. This allows us to override the JSON without modifying it (which would be overwritten daily).

```typescript
const VISION_MODEL_PATTERNS = [
  /qwen.*vl/i, // Matches all Qwen VL models
];
```

The pattern matches all current and future Qwen VL models: `qwen/qwen-vl-plus`, `qwen2.5-vl-32b-instruct`, etc.

## Change checklist
- [x] User facing
- [ ] Documentation update

- Resolves OPIK-2860

Manually tested in Playground:
- ✅ `qwen/qwen-vl-plus` with image: Run button enabled, model successfully analyzed image
- ✅ `qwen/qwen2.5-vl-32b-instruct` with image: Working correctly
- ✅ `qwen/qwen-2.5-coder-32b-instruct` (non-VL) with image: Run button correctly disabled with error message

author: avikivity
body:
parse() taking a list of elements is quadratic (during compile time) in that it generates recursive calls to itself, each time with one fewer parameter. The total size of the parameter lists in all these generated functions is quadratic in the initial parameter list size.

It's also exponential if we ignore inlining limits, since each .then() call expands to two branches - a ready future branch and a non-ready future branch. If the compiler did not give up, we'd have 2^list_len branches. For sure the compiler does not do so indefinitely, but the effort getting there is wasted.

Simplify by using a fold expression over the comma operator. Instead of passing the remaining parameter list in each step, we pass only the parameter we are processing now, making processing linear, and not generating unnecessary functions.

It would be better expressed using pack expansion statements, but these are part of C++26.

The largest offender is probably stats_metadata, with 21 elements.

dev-mode sstables.o:

   text	   data	    bss	    dec	    hex	filename
1760059	   1312	   7673	1769044	 1afe54	sstables.o.before
1745533	   1312	   7673	1754518	 1ac596	sstables.o.after

We save about 15k of text with presumably a corresponding (small) decrease in compile time.

Tiny compile time improvement, no backport necessary.

author: ti-chi-bot
body:
This is an automated cherry-pick of #2337

### What problem does this PR solve?

This PR introduces the necessary infrastructure to run integration tests against the TiDB "nextgen" architecture. Previously, our integration tests only supported the classic TiDB cluster setup. With the introduction of nextgen components and object storage (MinIO), a dedicated setup is required to validate TiCDC's compatibility and functionality with this new architecture.

Issue Number: close #2336 close #2561 close #1884

### What is changed and how it works?

This PR refactors the TiDB cluster startup and teardown scripts to support both classic and nextgen TiDB architectures for integration testing.

* **New Health Check Utilities:**
  * Added `tests/integration_tests/_utils/check_pd_health` to robustly check the health of a PD server using its `/pd/api/v1/health` endpoint.
  * Added `tests/integration_tests/_utils/check_tidb_health` to verify TiDB server readiness by executing a simple `SELECT` query via the `mysql` client.

* **Refactored TiDB Cluster Startup:**
  * The `tests/integration_tests/_utils/start_tidb_cluster` script is now a dispatcher, conditionally invoking either `start_tidb_cluster_classic` or `start_tidb_cluster_nextgen` based on the `NEXT_GEN` environment variable.
  * The original logic for starting a classic TiDB cluster has been moved into a new script: `tests/integration_tests/_utils/start_tidb_cluster_classic`.
  * A new script `tests/integration_tests/_utils/start_tidb_cluster_nextgen` has been added to provision a TiDB cluster with nextgen components. This includes:
    * Starting a MinIO server to act as an S3-compatible object storage backend.
    * Starting `pd-server-nextgen` instances (supporting multiple upstream PDs).
    * Starting `tikv-server-nextgen` instances, configured to use MinIO for storage.
    * Starting two `tidb-server-nextgen` instances: one for the `SYSTEM` keyspace and another for a user-defined `KEYSPACE_NAME`.
    * Starting a classic `pd-server`, `tikv-server`, and `tidb-server` for the downstream cluster.
    * Utilizing the new `check_pd_health` and `check_tidb_health` scripts to ensure component readiness.

* **Updated TiDB Cluster Teardown:**
  * `tests/integration_tests/_utils/stop_tidb_cluster` has been updated to correctly terminate `tidb-server-nextgen`, `tikv-server-nextgen`, `pd-server-nextgen`, and `minio` processes, along with their respective ports.

* **Enhanced Test Environment Preparation:**
  * `tests/integration_tests/_utils/test_prepare` now includes additional environment variables for:
    * Nextgen TiDB system ports and status addresses (`UP_TIDB_SYSTEM_PORT`, `UP_TIDB_SYSTEM_STATUS`).
    * MinIO configuration (`MINIO_API_PORT`, `MINIO_CONSOLE_PORT`, `MINIO_MC_ALIAS`, `MINIO_ROOT_USER`, `MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD`).
    * ANSI color codes for improved log readability.

* **Integration Test Runner Modifications:**
  * `tests/integration_tests/run.sh` now sources `_utils/test_prepare` and sets `export TICDC_NEWARCH=true` and `export CDC_BINARY=cdc.test` to enable nextgen testing by default for relevant tests.

### Check List

#### Tests

* Integration test

#### Questions

##### Will it cause performance regression or break compatibility?

No, this PR primarily introduces new test infrastructure for a different TiDB architecture. It does not affect the performance or compatibility of TiCDC itself.

##### Do you need to update user documentation, design documentation or monitoring documentation?

No, these changes are internal to the integration test suite and do not require updates to user, design, or monitoring documentation.

body:
Steps to reproduce:
===================
- Click on an orderline
- Then click on a detail inside it (e.g., eWallet Balance line)
- The numpad first opens and then closes right away

Issue:
======
- Clicking on a detail inside the orderline makes the numpad open and
  close at the same time
- This makes it impossible to use the numpad properly

Cause:
======
- The click from the child element also reaches the main orderline click
- Because of this, the numpad gets two clicks (open and close)

Fix:
====
- Added `stopPropagation` in the click handler to block event bubbling
- Now the numpad only reacts once and stays open as expected

**TinyVault** is a simple yet secure **local password manager** for beginners learning about file handling, encryption, and user input in Python.
It uses a **master password** to generate a cryptographic key for encrypting all stored credentials locally, ensuring privacy.
The project demonstrates secure password storage, encryption/decryption, and basic menu-based interaction.

**Features:**

* Master password–protected vault
* AES encryption via `cryptography.Fernet`
* Auto password generator (16 characters)
* Menu-driven console interface
* Safe add, view, list, and delete operations

**Why it's beginner-friendly:**

* Teaches modular Python coding practices
* Demonstrates basic cryptography and file handling
* No external servers or complex dependencies works locally

### Checklist:

Before submitting this PR, I have:

* [x] Created a new folder in `src/` using the format `akshat280706_password_manager`
* [x] Added `main.py` for core functionality
* [x] Included a `README.md` with setup and usage instructions
* [x] Added a `requirements.txt` listing dependencies
* [x] Tested the project locally to ensure it works as expected

### Project Details:

* **Language Used**: Python
* **External Dependencies**: `cryptography`
* **How to Run**:

  ```bash
  pip install cryptography
  python main.py
  ```

### additional Notes:

* The vault file is stored locally as `.tiny_vault.bin` in the user’s home directory.
* Passwords are never stored in plaintext.
* Suitable for anyone learning Python basics and security fundamentals.

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Currently in CEL PolicyAdmission we create mutating admission policy and binding and [sleep for a second](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/71fa43e37f198ae8035a96ff9f1c112b03b9e0fa/test/integration/apiserver/cel/admission_policy_test.go#L571-L572) and expect the policy and binding to be established.
Its not always the case as it might take more time to establish policy and binding and subsequent resources might have been created by tests without the binding in place and not generating any warning events and there are few flakes due to this.

In other part of the code in few tests we always make sure the that policy and binding established with help of polling. For example [createAndWaitReadyNamespacedWithWarnHandler](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/190c8c7abc5d6e6bb8ca2580bf67afa45d1b4929/test/integration/apiserver/cel/validatingadmissionpolicy_test.go#L3052-L3106)

author: dab246
body:
## Issue

#4128 

## Root cause

The interactor responsible for handling attachment downloads is created and managed inside the `SingleEmailController`. When the user navigates back to the mailbox, the email view is closed, which causes the `SingleEmailController` to be disposed. As a result, the interactor tied to it is also destroyed and can no longer continue processing. However, the download process still attempts to emit new events into a stream that has already been closed, leading to the error:

```console
Bad state: Cannot add new events after calling close
```

**Description**:
Improves type hinting in file_append_transaction.py to resolve numerous mypy --strict errors.
This PR addresses the type definitions for the FileAppendTransaction class, which allows mypy to properly analyze the file in strict mode.

- Add `from __future__ import annotations` for modern type handling.
- Add missing type hints for function arguments and return values (e.g., `_build_proto_body`, `execute`, `sign`, `freeze_with`).
- Import types required for hinting (like `Client`, `PrivateKey`, `TransactionReceipt`) inside a `TYPE_CHECKING` block to prevent circular imports.
- Resolve `[attr-defined]` errors by adding `assert` checks for `Optional` types in `freeze_with`.
- Specify generic type for `self._signing_keys` from `list` to `List[PrivateKey]`.
---

**Related issue(s)**:

Fixes #495 

**Notes for reviewer**:
This PR significantly reduces the `mypy --strict` error count for this file. The few remaining errors (like `[import-untyped]` or `[no-untyped-call]` from `super())` are due to other modules in the SDK not being fully typed yet, which was noted as out-of-scope in the issue.

Tested locally by running `mypy --strict` (after temporarily renaming the mypy.ini to avoid the encoding error). This confirmed that the changes successfully fixed the type errors as intended.

body:
This change allows Gemini chat completions within our application.

The big idea here is to allow users to create and store an API key in localStorage. Once a key is set, we can simply call `chat` to get a chat completion. The user will be prompted for a key if one is not set.

This can be used in the browser console or within JavaScript as:

```js
await chat('What is the capital of France?')
```

A test is included that sets an API key and confirms that Gemini is available.

> [!TIP]
> In order for tests to pass locally, you'll need the `GEMINI_API_KEY` environment variable set to a valid Gemini API key. These are free and can be generated via [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/api-keys).

> [!WARNING]
> This approach requires users to bring their own API keys and does not provide an ideal user experience. We could steal and repurpose these API keys. This is not appropriate for most applications, but it does provide a simple way to build a prototype application without designing a more complex backend.

author: back1ash
body:
## ✨ Key Features

### 1. Criticality System Redesign
- **Changed naming**: `A/B/C` → `Low/Middle/High`
- Added enum validation in CRD to ensure type safety
- Improved readability and maintainability

### 2. CPU Pool Management
- Per-core resource tracking with real-time utilization monitoring
- CPU usage calculated from RT settings: `(runtime / period) × 1000 millis`
- Supports core range specification (e.g., `"2-3"`, `"0,2,4"`)

### 3. Criticality-based Preemption
- **High priority**: Can preempt Middle and Low priority pods
- **Middle priority**: Can preempt Low priority pods
- **90% utilization threshold** triggers preemption
- Attempts core migration before eviction

### 4. RT Cgroup Application (Bug Fix)
- **Fixed**: RT settings now properly applied to containers
- Sets `cpu.rt_multi_runtime_us` per-core
- Sets `cpu.rt_period_us` and `cpuset.cpus`
- Works with both Burstable and BestEffort QoS

### 5. Bidirectional Runtime Escalation
- `runtime_low` → `runtime_hi` on eBPF overrun detection
- `runtime_hi` → `runtime_low` on CPU recovery (isCpuBusy=false)
- Batch revert of all RT pods when node pressure is resolved

### 6. Enhanced Eviction
- Adds `evicted=true` label before eviction for tracking
- Ignores CFS-only pods (no RT settings)

## 🧪 Testing

### Test Scenarios
**test-preemption-scenario.yaml**:
- 3 pods requesting same core (Core 2)
- High pod triggers preemption
- Middle/Low migrate to different cores

### Verified Results
- ✅ Preemption logic works correctly
- ✅ RT cgroup settings applied (cpu.rt_multi_runtime_us, cpuset.cpus)
- ✅ Core migration successful
- ✅ Works with BestEffort QoS pods

author: haithamlamki
body:
Standardizes the Supabase environment variable for the publishable key to `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` across the codebase and documentation. This resolves an inconsistency where the README specified `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` while the Supabase client and deployment guide used `VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, preventing the app from connecting to the backend.

- Updates `src/integrations/supabase/client.ts` to use `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`.
- Updates `src/docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` to align with this change.
- Adds a `.env.example` file to guide developers on required environment variables.

This fix is based on a detailed analysis provided by the user.

I've updated the preprocessing code to reduce the memory footprint. On top of this, the preprocessing also got a bit faster.

```
   293    581.4 MiB      0.0 MiB           1       Path(output_path).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   294    581.4 MiB      0.0 MiB           1       ad.settings.zarr_write_format = 3
   295   1069.4 MiB    488.1 MiB           1       _check_for_mismatched_keys(adata_paths)
   296   4622.3 MiB   3552.9 MiB           1       adata_concat = _lazy_load_anndatas(adata_paths, load_adata=load_adata)
   297   4110.3 MiB   -512.0 MiB           1       adata_concat.obs_names_make_unique()
   298   4110.3 MiB      0.0 MiB           1       chunks = _create_chunks_for_shuffling(adata_concat, n_obs_per_dataset, shuffle=shuffle)
   299                                         
   300   4110.3 MiB      0.0 MiB           1       if var_subset is None:
   301   4110.3 MiB      0.0 MiB           1           var_subset = adata_concat.var_names
   302                                         
   303   4110.3 MiB      0.0 MiB           1       for i, chunk in enumerate(tqdm(chunks)):
   304   4110.3 MiB      0.0 MiB           1           var_mask = adata_concat.var_names.isin(var_subset)
   305                                                 # np.sort: It's more efficient to access elements sequentially from dask arrays
   306                                                 # The data will be shuffled later on, we just want the elements at this point
   307   4180.2 MiB     69.9 MiB           1           adata_chunk = adata_concat[np.sort(chunk), :][:, var_mask].copy()
   308  64430.5 MiB  60250.3 MiB           1           adata_chunk = _persist_adata_in_memory(adata_chunk)
   309  64430.5 MiB      0.0 MiB           1           if shuffle:
   310                                                     # shuffle adata in memory to break up individual chunks
   311  64430.5 MiB      0.0 MiB           1               idxs = np.random.default_rng().permutation(np.arange(len(adata_chunk)))
   312  64430.5 MiB      0.0 MiB           1               adata_chunk = adata_chunk[idxs]
   313                                                 # convert to dense format before writing to disk
   314  64430.5 MiB      0.0 MiB           1           if should_denseify:
   315                                                     # Need to convert back to dask array to avoid memory issues when converting large sparse matrices to dense
   316                                                     adata_chunk = adata_chunk.copy()
   317                                                     adata_chunk.X = da.from_array(
   318                                                         adata_chunk.X, chunks=(zarr_dense_chunk_size, -1), meta=adata_chunk.X
   319                                                     ).map_blocks(lambda xx: xx.toarray(), dtype=adata_chunk.X.dtype)
   320                                         
   321  64430.5 MiB      0.0 MiB           1           if output_format == "zarr":
   322  64430.5 MiB      0.0 MiB           1               f = zarr.open_group(Path(output_path) / f"{DATASET_PREFIX}_{i}.zarr", mode="w")
   323  64559.8 MiB    129.3 MiB           2               write_sharded(
   324  64430.5 MiB      0.0 MiB           1                   f,
   325  64430.5 MiB      0.0 MiB           1                   adata_chunk,
   326  64430.5 MiB      0.0 MiB           1                   sparse_chunk_size=zarr_sparse_chunk_size,
   327  64430.5 MiB      0.0 MiB           1                   sparse_shard_size=zarr_sparse_shard_size,
   328  64430.5 MiB      0.0 MiB           1                   dense_chunk_size=zarr_dense_chunk_size,
   329  64430.5 MiB      0.0 MiB           1                   dense_shard_size=zarr_dense_shard_size,
   330  64430.5 MiB      0.0 MiB           1                   compressors=zarr_compressor,
   331                                                     )
   332                                                 elif output_format == "h5ad":
   333                                                     adata_chunk.write_h5ad(Path(output_path) / f"{DATASET_PREFIX}_{i}.h5ad", compression=h5ad_compressor)
   334                                                 else:

author: dev-jonathan
body:
## Issue Link / Problem Description
- Fixes #2385 - Testset generator not preserving persona and scenario metadata
- Improves synthetic data generation traceability by adding metadata fields to track query generation parameters
- Currently there's no way to trace which persona, style, and length settings were used for synthetic queries

## Changes Made
- Added metadata fields to `dataset_schema.py`:
  - `persona_name: Optional[str]`
  - `query_style: Optional[str]` 
  - `query_length: Optional[str]`
- Updated `single_hop/base.py` to populate these fields during synthetic data generation:
  ```python
  return SingleTurnSample(
      user_input=response.query,
      reference=response.answer,
      reference_contexts=[reference_context],
      persona_name=getattr(scenario.persona, "name", None),
      query_style=getattr(scenario.style, "name", None),
      query_length=getattr(scenario.length, "name", None),
  )
  ```
- Updated class documentation with descriptions for new fields

## Testing
### How to Test
- [x] Manual testing steps:
  1. Run synthetic data generation using SingleHopQuerySynthesizer
  2. Verify metadata fields are properly populated in generated samples
  3. Confirm values match the scenario settings (persona, style, length)
  4. Check backwards compatibility with existing code

## References
- Fixes Issue: #2385
- Documentation: Updated in `dataset_schema.py` docstring
- Implementation: Updated in `single_hop/base.py` for field population

## Screenshots/Examples
```python
# Example of generated sample with metadata:
{
    "user_input": "What are the key features of Python?",
    "reference": "Python is a versatile programming language...",
    "persona_name": "Student",
    "query_style": "POOR_GRAMMAR",
    "query_length": "MEDIUM"
}
```

Implementation using proxy to solve the issue of using `(number|string)[][]` as a domain.

Some scales are memoized to improve performance, which means their internal representation of the data array stay the same, while the array from the props change, this is not an issue for primitives or dates due to how D3 handles them using the `valueOf` fn.

body:
## What's Changed

This PR fixes two issues with the `uipath` CLI commands:

### 1. Pull Command Now Uses `coded-evals` Folder

**Problem**: The `uipath pull` command was downloading from the `evals/` folder, but `uipath push` uploads to `coded-evals/`. This meant files pushed weren't being pulled back.

**Solution**: Updated pull to download from `coded-evals/` folder, matching where push uploads files.

### 2. Added Interactive Conflict Detection

**Problem**: Both push and pull would silently overwrite files without warning users about conflicts.

**Solution**: Added interactive prompts that:
- Detect when local and remote files differ
- Show the local file's modification timestamp
- Ask users whether to overwrite or skip
- Use appropriate messaging for push vs pull operations

### Example User Experience

When pulling with conflicts:
```
File 'main.py' has different content on remote.
Local file last modified: 2025-10-28 04:53:14
Do you want to overwrite the local file with the remote version? [y/N]:
```

When pushing with conflicts:
```
File 'main.py' has different content on remote.
Local file last modified: 2025-10-28 04:57:23
Do you want to push and overwrite the remote file with your local version? [y/N]:
```

## Testing

Added comprehensive unit tests:
- ✅ 11 tests for conflict handlers (InteractiveConflictHandler, PushConflictHandler)
- ✅ 4 tests for push conflict detection
- ✅ 2 new tests for pull with coded-evals folder
- ✅ Updated existing pull tests to reflect new behavior

All tests passing.

Bumped version from `2.1.117` → `2.1.118`

body:
Applications frequently load configuration files and manager data on every render, causing repeated disk I/O and latency. This adds a lightweight, thread-safe TTL cache with a **consistent architecture and pattern for all modules** to reduce redundant reads.

## Implementation

**Cache utility** (`omf2/common/cache.py`)
- Dependency-free TTL cache using stdlib `time` + `threading.Lock`
- Opt-in via `OMF2_CACHE_TTL` env var (default: disabled)
- Legacy support for `OMF2_ADMIN_CACHE_TTL` (backwards compatible)
- `get_or_set()` pattern and `@cached` decorator for easy integration
- **Consistent pattern for use across all modules** (RegistryManager, CCUConfigLoader, etc.)

**Implementations completed:**

1. **Admin dashboard** (`omf2/ui/admin/admin_settings/dashboard_subtab.py`)
   - Extract config loading to `_load_config_file()` helper with cache lookup
   - Defensive import fallback—continues without cache if unavailable
   - No business logic changes

2. **RegistryManager** (`omf2/registry/manager/registry_manager.py`)
   - Added `_load_yaml_file_cached()` and `_load_json_file_cached()` helper methods
   - All 8 registry loading methods now use TTL cache:
     - Topics, Schemas, MQTT clients, Gateway, Workpieces, Modules, Stations, TXT controllers
   - Defensive fallback to direct loading if cache unavailable

3. **CCUConfigLoader** (`omf2/ccu/config_loader.py`)
   - Replaced simple dict cache with TTL cache
   - Created `_load_json_from_disk()` for actual disk I/O
   - All config loading methods now benefit from TTL caching:
     - Production workflows, settings, shopfloor layout, config metadata
   - Defensive fallback to direct loading if cache unavailable

**Usage pattern (consistent across all modules):**
```python
# Cache enabled with 60s TTL for all modules
export OMF2_CACHE_TTL=60

# Legacy admin-specific setting (still supported)
export OMF2_ADMIN_CACHE_TTL=60

# Usage pattern in code
from omf2.common.cache import get_cache

cache = get_cache()
data = cache.get_or_set("key", lambda: expensive_load())
```

## Testing

20 test cases in `tests/test_admin_cache.py` covering:
- TTL expiration behavior
- Cache enable/disable via both `OMF2_CACHE_TTL` and `OMF2_ADMIN_CACHE_TTL`
- Environment variable precedence
- Thread-safe operations
- Edge cases (missing keys, invalid TTL)

## Documentation

`docs/performance/cache.md` includes:
- Configuration and QA steps for all modules
- Integration examples for RegistryManager, CCUConfigLoader
- Consistent architecture pattern documentation
- Performance impact analysis
- Troubleshooting guide

## Modules with Cache Integration

The cache has been **fully implemented** in:
- ✅ Admin dashboard (implemented)
- ✅ **RegistryManager** (fully implemented with all file loading methods)
- ✅ **CCUConfigLoader** (fully implemented, replacing old dict cache)
- 📋 Other managers/loaders throughout the application (available for future integration)

## Safety

- Disabled by default (explicit opt-in)
- Thread-safe with lock-protected operations
- Graceful fallback on import failure
- Backwards compatible with legacy environment variable
- Available as common module for consistent use across all code paths
- No breaking changes to existing functionality

## Commit History

1. `chore(perf): add simple TTL cache util for admin`
2. `fix(admin): use cache for config loads in admin dashboard`
3. `docs: add admin cache performance notes`
4. `docs: improve admin_cache.md based on code review`
5. `refactor: move cache to common module for consistent architecture across all modules`
6. `feat: implement TTL cache for RegistryManager and CCUConfigLoader`

author: aaronstevenwhite
body:
# Fix FrameNet Lexical Unit Loading

Fixes https://github.com/aaronstevenwhite/glazing/issues/4

## Description

This PR fixes a critical data completeness issue where FrameNet lexical units were not being loaded during dataset conversion. All frames had empty `lexical_units` fields despite the raw FrameNet data containing 13,575 lexical units. This fix parses lexical units from `luIndex.xml` and properly associates them with their frames during conversion.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update

## Key Changes

### Lexical Unit Loading
- **Added LU parsing**: New methods to parse lexical units from `luIndex.xml`
- **Frame association**: LUs now properly associated with frames by `frame_id`
- **Complete metadata**: Preserves POS tags, annotation status, sentence counts, lexeme structures
- **High success rate**: 13,572 out of 13,575 LUs successfully parsed (99.98%)

### Validation Updates
- **Relaxed patterns**: Updated validators to handle real-world FrameNet data
- **Proper nouns**: Now accepts "April.n", "Monday.n"
- **Multi-word expressions**: Now accepts "a bit.n", "give up.v"
- **Special characters**: Now accepts "(can't) help.v", "American [N and S Am].n"

### Version Bump
- **Version**: 0.2.0 → 0.2.1 (patch release)
- **Updated**: All version references across package and documentation

## Problem

Frames had empty `lexical_units` fields after conversion:
```python
>>> from glazing.framenet.loader import FrameNetLoader
>>> loader = FrameNetLoader()
>>> index = loader.build_frame_index(loader.frames)
>>> frame = index.get_frame_by_name("Abandonment")
>>> len(frame.lexical_units)
0  # Should be 5!
```

The converter only parsed frame XML files and never loaded lexical unit data from `luIndex.xml`.

## Solution

### 1. Added LU Parsing Methods

**`_parse_lu_from_index()`** - Parse individual LU from XML element:
- Extract metadata (ID, name, POS, frame association, annotation status)
- Create lexemes from multi-word expressions
- Build sentence count statistics

**`convert_lu_index_file()`** - Convert entire `luIndex.xml`:
- Parse all LU elements from index
- Handle errors gracefully with warnings
- Return list of `LexicalUnit` models

### 2. Updated Frame Conversion

Modified `convert_frames_directory()` to:
1. Parse all frame XML files
2. Load lexical units from `luIndex.xml` (in parent directory)
3. Group LUs by `frame_id`
4. Associate LUs with their frames

### 3. Relaxed Validators

**Before:**
```python
LU_NAME_PATTERN = r"^[a-z][a-z0-9_\'-]*\.[a-z]+$"  # Too strict
LEXEME_NAME_PATTERN = r"^[A-Za-z][a-zA-Z0-9\'-]*$"  # Too strict
```

**After:**
```python
LU_NAME_PATTERN = r"^.+\.[a-z]+$"  # Permissive: anything.pos
LEXEME_NAME_PATTERN = r"^.+$"      # Permissive: any non-empty string
```

## Impact

### Before This Fix
- ✗ All frames had empty `lexical_units` fields
- ✗ Could not query frames by lexical unit name
- ✗ ~1,100+ LUs rejected by strict validators (91.3% success)
- ✗ Missing critical FrameNet data

### After This Fix
- ✓ All frames include their lexical units with complete metadata
- ✓ Can query frames by lexical unit name via frame index
- ✓ Only 3 LUs rejected (99.98% success)
- ✓ Complete FrameNet data coverage

### Example
```python
>>> from glazing.framenet.loader import FrameNetLoader
>>> loader = FrameNetLoader()
>>> index = loader.build_frame_index(loader.frames)
>>> frame = index.get_frame_by_name("Abandonment")
>>> len(frame.lexical_units)
5
>>> frame.lexical_units[0].name
'abandon.v'
>>> frame.lexical_units[0].pos
'V'
```

## Files Changed

### Core Implementation
- `src/glazing/framenet/converter.py` - Added LU parsing and frame association
- `src/glazing/framenet/types.py` - Relaxed validation patterns
- `src/glazing/cli/convert.py` - Updated CLI progress messages

### Tests
- `tests/test_framenet/test_converter.py` - Added 5 new LU parsing tests
- `tests/test_framenet/test_types.py` - Updated validation tests
- `tests/test_framenet/test_models.py` - Updated model tests

### Version and Documentation
- `pyproject.toml` - Version bump to 0.2.1
- `src/glazing/__version__.py` - Version bump to 0.2.1
- `CHANGELOG.md` - Added 0.2.1 entry
- `docs/` - Updated all version references (9 files)
- `.pre-commit-config.yaml` - Fixed Python 3.13 compatibility for hooks

## Testing

All tests pass with comprehensive coverage:
```bash
pytest tests/ -v --tb=short -q
# 1,338 tests passed, 81% code coverage

mypy --strict src/
# Success: no issues found

ruff check src/ tests/
# All checks passed

ruff format src/ tests/
# All files formatted correctly
```

## Compatibility

- ✓ Fully backwards compatible with v0.2.0
- ✓ No API changes
- ✓ No breaking changes
- ⚠️ Users must reconvert FrameNet data to populate lexical units:
  ```bash
  glazing init --force
  ```

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows project style guidelines (ruff, mypy)
- [x] All tests pass locally
- [x] Added tests for new functionality
- [x] Updated documentation
- [x] Updated CHANGELOG.md
- [x] Version bumped appropriately (0.2.0 → 0.2.1)
- [x] Release notes prepared

author: slashr
body:
## 🤖 Critical Fix for Autonomous PR Workflows

This PR fixes  to correctly document Codex review behavior, enabling fully autonomous PR workflows where AI agents can interact with Codex seamlessly.

### 🔍 Problem Discovered

While working on PRs #284 and #285, we discovered that the Codex review process was misunderstood, leading to:
- ❌ Missing actual review comments (inline code comments)
- ❌ Posting main-thread comments instead of inline replies (creating spam)
- ❌ Incorrect approval detection logic
- ❌ Cannot achieve autonomous PR workflows

### ✅ How Codex Actually Works

**When issues found:**
1. Posts **template comment** on main thread: "💡 Codex Review" (just a header)
2. Posts **inline code comments** with P1/P2/P3 badges ← THE ACTUAL REVIEW
3. Expects **inline replies** to each comment (not main thread comments)

**After fixes:**
4. Posts **NEW main comment**: "Didn't find any major issues. Breezy!" ← APPROVAL
5. This is a separate comment, not a reply to anything

### 📝 What Changed in .cursorrules

#### 1. Correct Review Structure Documentation
- Explained two-part review system (template + inline comments)
- Documented that template comment contains NO feedback
- Added commands to fetch inline code review comments specifically

#### 2. Inline Reply Workflow
- **Added**: How to reply to inline comments using comment ID
- **Removed**: Main thread reply examples (wrong approach)
- **Added**: API endpoint for posting inline replies

#### 3. Approval Detection
- **Fixed**: Check for "Didn't find any major issues" in NEW main comments
- **Added**: Time-based filtering to get recent comments only
- **Added**: Complete workflow script with all steps

#### 4. API Endpoint Documentation
- **Inline reviews**: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments`
- **Main thread**: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{pr}/comments`  
- **Reply inline**: `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/comments/{comment_id}/replies`

#### 5. Quick Reference Section
- Added pattern summary of Codex behavior
- Added key insight about two comment types
- Added complete command reference

### 🎯 Impact

This enables **fully autonomous PR workflows** where AI can:
1. ✅ Request Codex review
2. ✅ Parse inline code comments correctly (the real review)
3. ✅ Reply inline to each comment (proper context)
4. ✅ Detect approval accurately (new main comment)
5. ✅ Present clean PRs with all feedback addressed

### 📊 Verified Behavior

Based on actual Codex interactions in:
- **PR #284**: Received P1 inline comment about caching .terraform.lock.hcl
- **PR #285**: Received P1 inline comment about BASE_SHA handling
- Both received "Didn't find any major issues" approval after fixes

### 🚀 Next Steps

With this fix, future PRs will:
- Have proper inline comment replies (no spam)
- Correctly detect approval status
- Enable fully autonomous PR → Review → Fix → Approve → Merge workflows

---

**Testing:**
- ✅ All pre-commit hooks passing
- ✅ Documentation-only change (no functional impact)

This is a **critical documentation fix** for enabling autonomous workflows with Codex as the reviewing agent.

body:
**Refactored `feedback_callback` blocks**
Migrated the following logic blocks into their own `workflows` modules, and added unit tests for them:
* `atlas_update`
* `data_collection`
* `data_collection_group`
* `processing_job`

These workflows will potentially be shared between multiple data processing pipelines (SPA, tomo, and potentially CLEM), so suggestions on where to put them would be much appreciated.

**Modified `feedback_callback` entry points to return dictionary instead of boolean**
Some feedback callback functions will request for a message requeue, which our current setup doesn't support. By switching the workflows to return a dictionary, we can add a key to control whether the message gets requeued or not.

**Updated project package dependencies**
Some package dependencies were also updated:
* Removed the version lock on `stomp-py` from when `8.1.1` caused us issues
* Removed the FastAPI version lock from when there were conflicting `httpx` version dependencies
* Added `graypy` as an explicit package dependency, since we use it directly
* Removed `backports.entry_points_selectable` now that Python 3.9 has been dropped

body:
There was a tricky issue with the deployment using the Go hyp client, so instead we have to do this in Rust now. 

The celestia height must be chosen such that it contains at least one blob and the trusted state must be initialized to exactly the last blob from the trusted Celestia block. This PR solves this issue and aligns them perfectly.

When running the E2E or prover, we now have to deploy the ISM and Update using the ev-prover CLI. This is not yet automated.

Deployment command:

```
RUST_LOG="ev_prover=info" cargo run -p ev-prover create
```


Update command:
```
RUST_LOG="ev_prover=info" cargo run -p ev-prover update 0x726f757465725f69736d000000000000000000000000002a0000000000000001 0x726f757465725f61707000000000000000000000000000010000000000000000
```

body:
Adds Send, Receive, and Buy buttons with complete token selection and transaction flow.

## Key Changes
- **New Buttons**: Added Send, Receive (Get), and Buy buttons to the main interface
- **Token Selection**: Complete token selection UI with search and token list
- **Send Flow**: Full send transaction flow with confirmation screen
- **Estimated Fees**: Human-readable gas fee estimation component
- **Error Handling**: Improved transaction error parsing using viem
- **Token Hooks**: Added `useTokenCache` and `useTokenUsdPrices` hooks
- **UX Improvements**: Better button states, copy functionality, and visual feedback during transactions

## Technical Details
- Removed linked providers temporarily (to be added back)
- Form state persists after transactions for easier repeat sends
- Balance polling after successful transactions
- Better spacing and icon choices (credit card icon for Buy)

## 🎯 Overview
This PR adds the ability to save widget configurations directly to GitHub from the admin panel with one click!

## ✨ New Features

### 💾 Save to GitHub Button
- **One-click save** directly from admin panel to GitHub
- **Auto-commit** to `configs/` directory
- **Visual feedback** with success/error status
- **GitHub link** to view saved file immediately

### 🆔 Config ID Management
- **Config ID field** with validation (alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores)
- **Auto-generation** of random IDs on focus
- **Real-time validation** feedback
- **Enter key** support for quick save

### 🔧 Technical Implementation

#### New Files
- `functions/api/save-to-github.js` - GitHub API integration endpoint
- `GITHUB_SETUP.md` - Complete setup guide with troubleshooting

#### Modified Files
- `admin.html` - Added save button, config ID field, status display

### 📡 API Endpoint: /api/save-to-github

```javascript
POST /api/save-to-github

Body:
{
  "configId": "my-widget-config",
  "config": { /* widget configuration */ }
}

Response:
{
  "success": true,
  "configId": "my-widget-config",
  "message": "Configuration saved to GitHub successfully",
  "githubUrl": "https://github.com/TFWidgets/youtube-feed/blob/main/configs/my-widget-config.json",
  "embedCode": "<script src=\"https://youtube-feed.pages.dev/embed.js\" data-id=\"my-widget-config\"></script>"
}
```

### 🔐 Security & Configuration

Requires two environment variables in Cloudflare Pages:
- `GITHUB_TOKEN` - Personal Access Token with `repo` scope
- `GITHUB_REPO` - Repository name (e.g., `TFWidgets/youtube-feed`)

**Setup instructions**: See `GITHUB_SETUP.md`

### 🎨 Admin Panel UI Improvements

**Before:**
- Manual JSON copy-paste
- Create GitHub file manually
- Wait for deployment

**After:**
1. ✅ Fill in widget settings
2. ✅ Enter Config ID
3. ✅ Click "Save to GitHub"
4. ✅ Done! Config is live

### 🔄 Workflow

1. **User configures widget** in admin panel
2. **Enters Config ID** (or auto-generates)
3. **Clicks "💾 Save to GitHub"**
4. **API commits** to `configs/{configId}.json`
5. **Cloudflare Pages** auto-deploys (1-2 min)
6. **Widget works** at `embed.js?data-id={configId}`

### 🚀 Features

✅ **Direct GitHub commits** from browser
✅ **File create/update** with SHA detection
✅ **Atomic operations** - no manual git needed
✅ **Visual feedback** - success/error states
✅ **Link to GitHub** - view saved file instantly
✅ **Fallback support** - works with KV if GitHub not configured
✅ **Auto-embed code** - updates after save
✅ **Validation** - config ID sanitization
✅ **Random ID generation** - click to generate
✅ **Enter key** - quick save shortcut

### 🛡️ Error Handling

- ✅ Missing environment variables → fallback to KV
- ✅ Invalid GitHub token → clear error message
- ✅ Rate limiting → retry logic
- ✅ File conflicts → automatic merge with SHA
- ✅ Network errors → detailed error display

### 📖 Setup Guide

Complete setup instructions in `GITHUB_SETUP.md`:
1. Create GitHub Personal Access Token
2. Add to Cloudflare Pages environment variables
3. Test in admin panel
4. Done!

### 🧪 Testing Checklist

- ✅ Save new config file
- ✅ Update existing config file
- ✅ Invalid config ID validation
- ✅ GitHub token not configured (fallback)
- ✅ Invalid GitHub token (error handling)
- ✅ Network error handling
- ✅ Embed code auto-update
- ✅ GitHub URL link generation

### 💡 Benefits

1. **No manual git operations** - everything through UI
2. **Instant deployment** - Cloudflare auto-deploys
3. **Version control** - all changes tracked in Git
4. **Audit trail** - commit history shows all changes
5. **Easy rollback** - revert commits if needed
6. **Team friendly** - no need for repo access

### 🎯 Use Case

**Admin workflow:**
1. Customer requests widget customization
2. Open admin panel
3. Configure widget
4. Enter customer ID as config ID
5. Save to GitHub
6. Send customer embed code
7. Customer pastes on their site
8. Done! ✨

### 🔗 Related

- Builds on PR #1 (Admin Panel)
- Uses PR #2 (API Integration)
- Enables direct config management
- Removes manual file creation step

## 🌐 Demo

Once deployed:

author: peter-lawrey
body:
This PR brings **Chronicle-Test-Framework** in line with current Chronicle engineering standards. It introduces an opt-in **`-P code-review`** quality gate, updates contributor guidance to **ISO-8859-1** text policy, moves project docs under `src/main/docs/`, and makes a series of small but meaningful robustness and hygiene fixes across the codebase. No public APIs are changed.

---

## Why

* **Consistent quality bar** across OpenHFT repos (Checkstyle/SpotBugs/PMD/JaCoCo with shared rules).
* **Clearer contributor guidance** (ISO-8859-1 text policy; corrected doc links).
* **More robust test helpers** (safer logging, locale-safe formatting, correct stream usage).
* **Housekeeping** (copyright years, remove stale backup).

---

## What changed

### 1) Contributor docs

* **`AGENTS.md`**

  * Switch language policy from *ASCII-7* → **ISO-8859-1** (retain “no smart quotes / NBSP” guidance).
  * Update references to **`src/main/docs/decision-log.adoc`** and **`src/main/docs/project-requirements.adoc`**.
* **`README.adoc`**

  * New **“Quality Checks”** section with `mvn -q -P-code-review verify` usage.
  * Minor formatting clean-ups (consistent comment spacing; wrapped long lines).

### 2) Build / Quality gate

* **New opt-in profile `code-review`** (kept *off* by default):

  * `maven-checkstyle-plugin` **3.6.0** + `com.puppycrawl.tools:checkstyle` **8.45.1** with shared **`net/openhft/quality/checkstyle/checkstyle.xml`**.
  * `spotbugs-maven-plugin` **4.8.6.6** + `com.h3xstream:findsecbugs-plugin` **1.14.0**; repository-local **`src/main/config/spotbugs-exclude.xml`** scaffold.
  * `maven-pmd-plugin` **3.28.0** with **`src/main/config/pmd-exclude.properties`**.
  * `jacoco-maven-plugin` **0.8.14** wired for `prepare-agent`, `report`, and `check` with project thresholds (line **0.846**, branch **0.707**) in default build; same goals run under `code-review` profile.
  * Add `com.github.spotbugs:spotbugs-annotations` (**provided**) to enable precise suppressions.
* Remove obsolete `pom.xml.versionsBackup`.

### 3) Documentation layout

* Move **`src/main/adoc/project-requirements.adoc` → `src/main/docs/project-requirements.adoc`** (no content changes).

### 4) Code hygiene & robustness (no API surface changes)

* **Log sanitisation** to avoid CR/LF injection in test utilities:

  * `VanillaExceptionTracker`, `CodeStructureVerifier`, `ProxyConnection`, `TcpProxy`, `MappedFileUtil`, `InternalJavaProcessBuilder`: strip `\r`/`\n` from values used in log messages.
* **Locale-stable formatting & casing**:

  * Use `Locale.ROOT` in `Standard*Accumulator` formatting; replace `%n` / explicit padding; use `Locale.ROOT` for case transforms where relevant.
* **Correct stream usage & diagnostics**:

  * `InternalJavaProcessBuilder#getProcessStdOut` now reads from `getInputStream()` (was incorrectly reading `getErrorStream()`).
  * Safer `ProcessBuilder` invocation with pre-split args (no shell expansion) and improved logging of child process output.
* **Static-analysis suppressions where intentional**:

  * Add targeted `@SuppressFBWarnings` and PMD suppressions with justifications (e.g. deliberate `System.gc()` in test utilities; exposing provided maps for test tracking; path parsing in ArchUnit integration).
* **Minor clean-ups / correctness nits**:

  * Fix lambda parentheses in `ProductUtil` to avoid PMD false positives.
  * Adjust `SeriesUtil#isPrime` cast order.
  * Use `@since 2006-2025` copyright headers.
  * Small readability tweaks (`padRight` helpers, clearer local variables, remove dead locals, tighten visibilities, use try-with-resources).

---

## How to use

```bash
# Normal CI-equivalent build (unchanged)
mvn -q verify

# Run pre-merge quality gate locally (strongly recommended)
mvn -q -Pcode-review verify
```

---

## Compatibility & Impact

* **Source/ABI:** No public API changes; all modifications are internal or documentation-only.
* **Build:** New profile is opt-in; default `mvn verify` still works. Adds a `provided` SpotBugs annotations dep (no runtime impact).
* **Text policy:** The ISO-8859-1 guidance affects documentation and contributor content. Source code continues to enforce ASCII in string literals per our Checkstyle rules.

---

## Verification

* Full `mvn -q -Pcode-review verify` green locally (unit tests, Checkstyle, PMD, SpotBugs+FindSecBugs, JaCoCo thresholds).
* Smoke-tested `InternalJavaProcessBuilder` logging improvements.
* Confirmed moved docs are referenced correctly from `AGENTS.md`.

---

## Risks & Mitigations

* **Stricter checks may fail downstream forks.** The `code-review` profile is optional; downstreams can opt-in when ready.
* **Policy mismatch (ISO-8859-1 vs ASCII source).** Intentionally kept; we’ll clarify in a follow-up doc that source files remain ASCII-only while prose may use Latin-1.

---

## Follow-ups

* Populate `src/main/config/spotbugs-exclude.xml` with targeted, justified entries as needed.
* Extend docs with a minimal “Getting Started with `code-review`” section, and a short note on encoding policy for docs vs source.

author: fbuzila-g2
body:
## Problem
Upbound AWS provider v2.x managed resources (`elasticache.aws.m.upbound.io`) **do NOT support** the `namespace` field in `writeConnectionSecretToRef`. The secret namespace is automatically determined from the resource's `metadata.namespace` field.

However, the current JSON schema validation requires both `name` and `namespace` fields in the `writeConnectionSecretToRef` block, causing CI/CD failures when deploying Upbound Cluster resources.

**Error from CI/CD validation**:
```
⚠️ Invalid: elasticache.aws.m.upbound.io/v1beta1 Cluster tracking-api-cache-upbound
problem validating schema. Check JSON formatting: jsonschema: '/spec/writeConnectionSecretToRef' 
does not validate with https://raw.githubusercontent.com/g2crowd/kubernetes-json-schema/refs/heads/main/schemas/cluster_v1beta1.json#/properties/spec/properties/writeConnectionSecretToRef/required: 
missing properties: 'namespace'
```

## Root Cause
API differences between provider types:
- **crossplane-contrib provider** (`cache.aws.crossplane.io`): Requires explicit `namespace` field
- **Upbound provider** (`elasticache.aws.m.upbound.io`): Does NOT support `namespace` field (errors if present)

This creates a conflict where:
- Runtime: Upbound provider rejects `namespace` field
- CI/CD: Schema validation requires `namespace` field

## Solution
Make the `namespace` field **optional** by removing it from the `required` array in the `writeConnectionSecretToRef` schema definition.

**Before**:
```json
"required": [
  "name",
  "namespace"
]
```

**After**:
```json
"required": [
  "name"
]
```

Also updated the description of the `namespace` field to clarify it's optional for Upbound managed resources.

## Benefits
✅ Fixes CI/CD validation errors for Upbound Cluster resources  
✅ Enables PE-418 migration from crossplane-contrib to Upbound providers  
✅ Maintains backward compatibility - crossplane-contrib resources can still provide namespace  
✅ Aligns schema with Upbound provider runtime behavior  
✅ Fixes this for all future Upbound Cluster resources (not just PE-418)

## Testing
After merge:
1. This PR will unblock configuration repo PR #2409 from passing CI/CD checks
2. Upbound Cluster resources without `namespace` field will pass validation
3. Resources with `namespace` field will still pass (backward compatible)

## Impact
- **No breaking changes**: Resources can still provide `namespace` if needed
- **Fixes**: All Upbound Cluster v1beta1 resources across all environments
- **Enables**: Migration from crossplane-contrib provider to Upbound provider

## Related
- **Jira**: [PE-418](https://g2crowd.atlassian.net/browse/PE-418) - ElastiCache infinite reconciliation migration
- **Blocked PR**: configuration#2409 (waiting on this schema fix)
- **Provider Documentation**: [Upbound Provider AWS](https://marketplace.upbound.io/providers/upbound/provider-family-aws)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

[PE-418]: https://g2crowd.atlassian.net/browse/PE-418?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

author: christiangeie
body:
**Summary**

This PR removes the `linux/s390x` target from the multi-architecture Docker build matrix.

**Reason**

The `s390x` (IBM Z) architecture requires building `pydantic-core` from source using Rust.
Due to missing Rustup support for `s390x-unknown-linux-musl` and extremely long build times under QEMU emulation, the CI builds on GitHub Actions frequently stalled or failed.

Since we do not actively deploy to IBM Z or LinuxONE environments, maintaining this architecture is unnecessary for our release process.

**Changes**

- Removed linux/s390x from the `PLATFORMS` list in the build matrix
- All other supported architectures (`amd64`, `arm64`, `ppc64le`) remain unchanged
- No functional or runtime changes to the application itself

**Notes**

If native `s390x` support is needed in the future, it can be reintroduced via a dedicated build job using a native `s390x` runner instead of QEMU emulation.

This is implementing preferences API for Web Publications so that we can improve the prototype Navigator. 

It implements: 

- zoom
- font-family
- font-weight
- text-align
- hyphens
- text-normalization
- line-height
- paragraph spacing
- paragraph indent
- letter-spacing
- word-spacing
- ligatures
- ruby annotations

Zoom is effective if the browser supports zoom, there is no fallback in case it does not. 

All other preferences are tied to feature `displayTransformability` in `publication.metadata.accessibility`

At the moment, an internal Stylesheet is used to set properties following Readium CSS pattern. This is probably evolving in the future, with Readium CSS providing a proper stylesheet for web publications.

author: joshsc63
body:
This PR consolidates **8 community contributions** that enhance aubio's compatibility with modern systems and development tools. All changes are minimal, targeted fixes with preserved original authorship.

## Summary of Included Fixes

### 1. NumPy 1.19+ / GCC 14 Compatibility ⭐
**Author:** @joshsc63
**Changes:** `setup.py` (cross-platform compiler flags)
**Impact:** Fixes compilation with NumPy 1.26.4+ and GCC 14

Adds `-Wno-incompatible-pointer-types` compiler flag for GCC/Clang to suppress false positive warnings with NumPy 1.19+'s const-qualified function signatures.

```python
extra_compile_args = []
if not sys.platform.startswith('win'):
    extra_compile_args = ['-Wno-incompatible-pointer-types']
```

---

### 2. PR #427 - FFmpeg 8.0 Compatibility ⭐
**Author:** Bernd Kuhls (@bkuhls)
**Changes:** `src/io/source_avcodec.c` (4 lines)

Fixes compilation with FFmpeg 7.0+ which removed `AV_INPUT_BUFFER_MIN_SIZE`. Adds version-gated fallback value.

```c
+#elif LIBAVUTIL_VERSION_INT >= AV_VERSION_INT(57, 28, 100)
+// FFmpeg 7.0+ removed AV_INPUT_BUFFER_MIN_SIZE, use safe fallback
+#define AUBIO_AVCODEC_MAX_BUFFER_SIZE 16384
```

**Impact:** Fixes build failures on systems with FFmpeg 7.0/8.0+ (Arch Linux, macOS with Homebrew)
**Fallback Value:** 16384 bytes (16KB) - safe default matching previous behavior

---

### 3. PR #418 - FFmpeg Channel Layout API ⭐
**Author:** Lluc Simó (@acrilique)
**Fixes:** #397
**Changes:** `src/io/source_avcodec.c` (2 lines)

Updates to modern FFmpeg channel layout API, replacing deprecated `{in,out}_channel_layout` with `{in,out}_chlayout`.

```c
-av_opt_set_chlayout(avr, "in_channel_layout",  &input_layout,  0);
-av_opt_set_chlayout(avr, "out_channel_layout", &output_layout, 0);
+av_opt_set_chlayout(avr, "in_chlayout",  &input_layout,  0);
+av_opt_set_chlayout(avr, "out_chlayout", &output_layout, 0);
```

**Impact:** Prevents deprecation warnings with FFmpeg 7.0+
**Reference:** Similar to [mpv-player/mpv#13662](https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/pull/13662)

---

### 4. PR #416 - Python Regex Raw Strings ⭐
**Author:** Pink Serenity (@PinkSerenity)
**Changes:** `python/lib/gen_code.py` (2 lines)

Fixes Python 3.x deprecation warnings by using raw strings for regex patterns.

```python
-paramregex = re.compile('(\w+ ?\*?).*')
+paramregex = re.compile(r'(\w+ ?\*?).*')
```

**Impact:** Python 3.x best practices, prevents UTF-8 encoding issues on non-English systems

---

### 5. PR #407 - Big-Endian FLAC Support ⭐
**Author:** Thomas Perale (@tperale)
**Changes:** `src/io/sink_flac.c` (3 lines)

Adds missing `SWAPS` macro definition for big-endian architectures when libFLAC is enabled.

```c
+// swap endian of a short
+#define SWAPS(x) ((x & 0xff) << 8) | ((x & 0xff00) >> 8)
```

**Impact:** Fixes build failures on MIPS, PowerPC, and other big-endian systems
**Validation:** Verified by Buildroot CI

---

### 6. PR #371 - MSVC UTF-8 Encoding ⭐
**Author:** lidotcircle (@lidotcircle)
**Related:** #293, #316
**Changes:** `setup.py` (4 lines)

Forces MSVC compiler to use UTF-8 encoding when building Python extensions on Windows.

```python
+if sys.platform == 'win32':
+    extra_compile_args += [ '/utf-8' ]
```

**Impact:** Fixes Windows builds on non-English locales (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, etc.)

---

### 7. PR #321 - Documentation Typo Fix ⭐
**Author:** Tim Gates (@timgates42)
**Changes:** Multiple header files (7 lines)

Fixes spelling: `successfull` → `successful` in documentation comments.

**Impact:** Improves documentation quality
**Status:** Previously approved by community

---

### 8. PR #411 - Demo Script Output Fix ⭐
**Author:** Stefan Sauer (@ensonic)
**Changes:** `python/demos/demo_notes.py` (1 line)

Fixes unused variable in demo - actually prints the detected note string.

```python
-note_str = notes_o.get_last_note()
+print("note_str:", notes_o.get_last_note())
```

**Impact:** Improves demo usability

---

## Files Changed

```
9 files changed, 28 insertions(+), 13 deletions(-)

 python/demos/demo_notes.py |  2 +-
 python/lib/gen_code.py     |  4 ++--
 setup.py                   |  8 ++++++++
 src/effects/pitchshift.h   |  4 ++--
 src/effects/timestretch.h  |  6 +++---
 src/io/sink_flac.c         |  3 +++
 src/io/source_avcodec.c    |  8 ++++++--
 src/pitch/pitch.h          |  4 ++--
```

---

## Compatibility Matrix

This consolidated PR enhances compatibility across modern systems:

| System/Tool | Improvement | Priority |
|-------------|-------------|----------|
| **NumPy 1.26.4+** | ✅ GCC 14 compilation | Critical |
| **FFmpeg 7.0/8.0+** | ✅ Version compatibility + API update | Critical |
| **Python 3.x** | ✅ Raw string regex patterns | High |
| **Big-endian** | ✅ MIPS, PowerPC FLAC support | High |
| **Windows MSVC** | ✅ UTF-8 encoding (CJK locales) | High |
| **Documentation** | ✅ Fixed typos | Medium |
| **Demos** | ✅ Improved usability | Medium |

---

## Testing

### Backward Compatibility
✅ **Yes** - All changes are backward compatible
- No breaking changes
- Minimal modifications to existing code
- Version-gated where appropriate (FFmpeg)

### Platform Testing
- ✅ **Linux:** Ubuntu 24.04, Debian Trixie (GCC 14.0.1, 14.2)
- ✅ **NumPy:** 1.26.4 compatibility verified
- ✅ **FFmpeg:** 6.x, 7.0, 8.0+ compatibility
- ✅ **Python:** 3.x regex warnings resolved
- ✅ **Big-endian:** Validated by Buildroot CI (MIPS, PowerPC)
- ✅ **Windows:** MSVC UTF-8 builds functional
- ✅ **Demos:** All demo scripts operational

### CI Status
The `linux_nodeps` build passes, proving the Python extension fix works correctly.

---

## Why Consolidate?

These PRs have been open for extended periods (some since 2020) without maintainer review:

- **PR #427** - Opened Oct 5, 2025 (FFmpeg 8.0 fix)
- **PR #418** - Opened Feb 26, 2025
- **PR #416** - Opened Feb 24, 2025
- **PR #411** - Opened Oct 13, 2024
- **PR #407** - Opened Sep 22, 2024
- **PR #371** - Opened Aug 25, 2022
- **PR #321** - Opened Nov 27, 2020
- **This PR** - Opened Oct 28, 2025

**Benefits of Consolidation:**
- ✅ Speeds up integration of important community fixes
- ✅ Maintains original authorship (git history preserved)
- ✅ Reduces review overhead for maintainers
- ✅ Each fix is small, focused, and low-risk
- ✅ Production-tested by community members
- ✅ Benefits entire aubio ecosystem

---

## Credits

Huge thanks to all contributors who made these excellent fixes:

- **@joshsc63** - NumPy 1.26.4+ / GCC 14 compatibility (PR author & submitter)
- **@bkuhls** (Bernd Kuhls) - FFmpeg 8.0 compatibility
- **@acrilique** (Lluc Simó) - FFmpeg channel layout API update
- **@PinkSerenity** (Pink Serenity) - Python regex improvements
- **@tperale** (Thomas Perale) - Big-endian FLAC support
- **@lidotcircle** - Windows UTF-8 encoding
- **@timgates42** (Tim Gates) - Documentation fixes
- **@ensonic** (Stefan Sauer) - Demo improvements

---

## Related Issues & PRs

**Fixes:**
- #397 - FFmpeg deprecated channel layout options

**Related:**
- #293, #316 - Windows UTF-8 encoding issues

**Includes:**
- #427, #418, #416, #407, #371, #321, #411 (community PRs)

**Supersedes:**
- #429 (closed - consolidated into this PR)

---

## Checklist

- [x] No breaking changes
- [x] Backward compatible
- [x] Minimal code modifications
- [x] All original authors credited
- [x] Tested on multiple platforms
- [x] Improves system compatibility
- [x] Production-validated
- [x] Git history preserves authorship
- [x] FFmpeg 6.x/7.0/8.0+ compatible

---

**Maintainer Note:** This PR consolidates 8 community contributions with preserved commit authorship. All changes are minimal, targeted fixes that enhance aubio's compatibility with modern development environments.

author: spcomb
body:
Fixes https://github.com/qmsk/esp/issues/86

New `leds` -> `interface_setup = true` mode to replace the `leds_tx()` -> `i2s_out_setup()` with a one-time `i2s_out_setup()`. This only works with one `leds` per interface, and does not work if sharing interfaces between multiple `leds` instances. This is currently only supported for I2S interfaces, and has no effect for other interfaces.

This allows a new async mode of operation where `leds_interface_i2s_tx()` now calls `i2s_out_write_*()` -> `i2s_out_start()` instead of `i2s_out_flush()`, which fills the I2S DMA buffer and starts the DMA/TX as previously, but does not wait for it to complete. The next loop -> tx can then start filling up the DMA buffer as DMA descriptors are freed up by the EOF interrupt, and waits for the previous TX to complete before starting the new TX using the recycled DMA buffer/descriptors.

This significantly increases the efficiency of the LEDS I2S interface, and it can now reach framerates close to the theoretical maximum (`800kbps / (24-bits-per-pixel × pixel-count)`).

body:
## Summary

Fixed TWO critical issues in MoAI-ADK:

1. **Skill Double Invocation Pattern** - Eliminated redundant Skill() loading before tool calls
2. **Command Completion Pattern** - Added AskUserQuestion rule for all Alfred commands

### Issue 1: Skill Double Invocation

The 'moai-alfred-interactive-questions' skill was being invoked TWICE in succession:
- Problem: Skill() loading followed by AskUserQuestion tool
- Result: 2-5 second delay + 1,600 wasted tokens per command

**Root Cause**: Mixed documentation pattern where both 'load Skill()' and 'use AskUserQuestion' instructions coexist

**Solution**: Standardized all 125 instances across 40 files (19 active + 21 templates)
- Changed from: `Call Skill("moai-alfred-interactive-questions")`
- Changed to: `AskUserQuestion tool (documented in moai-alfred-interactive-questions skill)`

### Issue 2: Command Completion Pattern

Added critical rule to CLAUDE.md: When ANY Alfred command completes, ALWAYS use AskUserQuestion to ask what to do next.

**Implementation**:
- /alfred:0-project completion → Use AskUserQuestion for next step
- /alfred:1-plan completion → Use AskUserQuestion for next step
- /alfred:2-run completion → Use AskUserQuestion for next step
- /alfred:3-sync completion → Use AskUserQuestion for next step

**Rules**:
✅ Always use AskUserQuestion tool (not prose suggestions)
✅ Provide 3-4 clear options
✅ Use user's conversation_language
❌ Never suggest next steps in prose
❌ Never invoke Skill() before tool calls

### Changes Summary

**Files Changed**: 42 total
- Active .claude/ files: 19 files (125 replacements)
- Template files: 21 files (58 replacements)
- CLAUDE.md files: 2 files (new Command Completion Pattern section)

**Total Statistics**: 
- Skill invocation fixes: 183 insertions(+), 183 deletions(-)
- Command completion pattern: 132 new insertions

### Test Plan
- ✅ Verify `/alfred:0-project` skill invocation appears once (not twice)
- ✅ Verify next step selection uses AskUserQuestion (not prose)
- ✅ Validate ~2-5 second performance improvement
- ✅ Check no regression in other Alfred commands

### Related Issues

Resolves:
- Double skill invocation pattern issue
- Missing AskUserQuestion rule for command completion

This PR improves the Socket Basics SAST ruleset defaults and updates documentation to reflect the current state of the project:

- **Reduced false positives** across all language rulesets (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, PHP, Ruby, Go, Kotlin, Scala, Swift, Rust, C/C++, .NET, Elixir, Erlang, Objective-C)

- **Enhanced Java and PHP rulesets** with additional vulnerability patterns and reduced noise
- **Updated default enabled rules** in connectors.yaml to focus on high-confidence, actionable findings

### Documentation Updates
- **Replaced all Semgrep references with OpenGrep** - the actual SAST engine used by Socket Basics
- **Corrected installation instructions** - Socket Basics is not published to PyPI and must be installed from source using `pip install -e .`
- **Added OpenGrep installation guide** with official installer command
- Updated installation documentation across local-installation.md, local-install-docker.md, pre-commit-hook.md, and github-action.md

### Other Changes
- Added vulnerable app test submodules (govwa, play-webgoat) to .gitmodules
- Updated .gitignore for better Python development workflow
- Version bump to reflect ruleset improvements
