Replaces the previous phone-based OTP authentication system with a standard email and password system using Supabase Auth.

This change addresses the user's request for a completely free authentication solution.

body:
AbstractReader pads the data with zeros by default.
This is not always ideal, especially for quaternions, where zero quaternions can be problematic (quaternions' norms should be equal to 1).
In this PR, this is solved by manually adjusting the padded values after the default zero-padding.

- **Minimal tool calls** (removed all backgrounds/borders for ultra-clean aesthetic)
- **Refined markdown typography** (14px base, compact spacing, subtle colors)
- **Proper alignment** (fixed copy button positioning and text/tool alignment)

## Performance Improvements

### Markdown Rendering: ~200ms → Instant ⚡
- **Removed Shiki** syntax highlighting for chat (async WASM = slow)
- Switched from `MarkdownHooks` → synchronous `ReactMarkdown`
- Chat now renders instantly alongside tool calls
- Save Shiki for file viewer later (where colors matter more)

## Visual Design Changes

### 1. Tool Calls - Ultra Minimal
- Removed all backgrounds and left borders
- Only hover opacity change (70%) for interaction feedback
- Content comes first, chrome disappears

### 2. Visual Anchors - Scanability
Added colored pills for key identifiers:
- **File paths**: Muted pill with file icon
- **Bash commands**: Primary-colored pill (blue)
- **Grep patterns**: Info-colored pill (blue)
- **Edit stats**: Success/destructive colors for +/- lines

### 3. Markdown Typography - IDE Density
**Jony Ive principles applied**:
- Code blocks: 12px font, 8px/12px padding (50% reduction)
- Headers: Gestalt proximity (more space above, less below)
- H1/H2: Bold (700) for scanability as visual anchors
- H3-H6: Semibold (600) for hierarchy
- Subtle colors: 92% foreground opacity (easier on eyes)
- Backgrounds: 50-60% opacity (gentle, not harsh)

### 4. Copy Button - Icon Only
- Icon-only design (no "Copy" text)
- 14x14px, muted until hover
- Green checkmark when copied
- Properly aligned with code content padding (top-3 right-4)

### 5. Text Alignment Fix
- Text blocks now have `px-2` to match tool call headers
- Everything aligns perfectly on left edge

## Architecture Improvements

### New Markdown System
Created reusable markdown components:
- `MarkdownRenderer.tsx` - Core component (security, GFM support)
- `ChatMarkdown.tsx` - Chat-specific wrapper with IDE typography
- `global.css` - Vanilla CSS styles (Tailwind v4 doesn't support @apply)

### Refactored Tool Renderers
- Simplified all 15+ tool renderers
- Removed redundant styling patterns
- Added colored pills consistently
- Better error handling with visual feedback

## Files Changed

**New files**:
- `src/components/markdown/MarkdownRenderer.tsx`
- `src/components/markdown/ChatMarkdown.tsx`
- `src/components/markdown/index.ts`
- `CHAT_REDESIGN.md` (design documentation)

**Updated files**:
- All tool renderers (15+ files) - visual anchors + minimal design
- `src/global.css` - 235 lines of markdown typography
- `TextBlock.tsx` - uses new ChatMarkdown
- `chatTheme.ts` - alignment fixes
- `BaseToolRenderer.tsx` - removed backgrounds/borders

## Test Plan

- [x] Markdown renders instantly with tools (no delay)
- [x] Copy button aligned with code block padding
- [x] Text blocks align with tool call headers
- [x] Code blocks are compact (12px, tight padding)
- [x] Headers have proper Gestalt proximity spacing
- [x] Visual anchors (pills) make tools scannable
- [x] All colors are subtle (no pure white/black)
- [x] Tool calls have minimal chrome (no backgrounds)

## Design Philosophy

> "Simplicity is about subtracting the obvious and adding the meaningful." - Jony Ive

Every design decision serves one purpose: **Help users find information faster**.

- More space above headers = Visual section breaks
- Less space below headers = Headers group with content
- Bold top headers = Visual landmarks when scrolling
- Small code = Doesn't dominate the page
- Icon-only buttons = Action speaks for itself
- Subtle colors = Easy on eyes during long sessions

BREAKING CHANGE: The new format for comapeocat files is incompatible with the previous one. This version of the app will not be able to import `.comapeocat` files that were not created with the new `npx comapeocat` tool.

This updates @mapeo/default-categories to v6, which are the same categories (with some minor fixes) but in the new `comapeocat` format. The new format only includes SVG icons, and only of one size (currently exposed as `medium` via the core API).

The only place we use category icons, I think, is in `PresetIcon.tsx`. For backwards-compatibility (existing projects which only have PNG icons) this will fall-back to trying to load a PNG icon if loading an SVG icon fails.

The new format and the core updates fix various issues with category imports and translations.

body:
PSR-4 config now supports registering multiple paths for a single namespace, enabling fallback directory resolution similar to Composer's autoloader behavior.

## Changes

- **Autoloader constructor**: Normalizes config to handle both `string` and `array` path values, maintaining backward compatibility
- **`getPath()` method**: Returns `array` of candidate paths instead of `?string`, allowing callers to check multiple locations
- **`spl_autoload_register` callback**: Iterates through returned paths array, loading first existing file
- **`realpath_all()` fix**: Preserves leading `/` for absolute paths (fixed pre-existing bug causing 12 test failures)

## Example

```php
// Single path (backward compatible)
$config = ['App\\' => 'src'];

// Multiple paths (new functionality)
$config = ['App\\' => ['src', 'lib', 'vendor/custom']];

$autoloader = new Autoloader($rootDir, $config);
$paths = $autoloader->getPath('App\\MyClass');
// Returns: ['/root/src/MyClass.php', '/root/lib/MyClass.php', '/root/vendor/custom/MyClass.php']

// Autoloader loads first existing file
```

## Test Coverage

Added 7 tests covering multi-path scenarios including duplicate class handling, non-existent directories, and backward compatibility.

### Summary
This PR fixes persistent Railway Postgres connection failures caused by conflicting sslmode parameters and incomplete SSL validation handling in the Node/pg Pool configuration. Connections now work out of the box with self-signed certificates, without requiring `?sslmode=` params in DATABASE_URL.

### Details
- Strips any `?sslmode=` params from DATABASE_URL via `stripSslmodeParam()`; the server now ignores sslmode query strings.
- Always enables SSL (`rejectUnauthorized: false, checkServerIdentity: () => undefined`) for all non-local connections (Railway, cloud, etc).
- Applies consistent SSL config to all connection points: main server Pool, migrate/reset scripts.
- Major upgrade to connection-startup logging (shows when certificate validation is bypassed; clearer error hints for failures).
- Updates `.env.example` and documentation with the improved, simpler setup—no more `?sslmode` confusion for deployers.
- Users can simply paste their Railway database string; SSL settings are safe-by-default and require no manual intervention.

author: jacobhinkle
body:
Prior to this change we have two separate systems for computing parallel extents:
1) `ParallelDimensionMap` is used to compute dimensions for generating the CUDA kernel
2) The `KernelExecutor` uses another system including `ParallelExtentMap` which gathers all of the extents of IDs in the promoted group for each paralleltype, and computes the max extent across all those.

This is redundant: we should have a centralized place to find the following information:
1) Extent expressions for use in generated code
2) Extent expressions for evaluation in the executor
3) Index expressions used in generated code

In the future, I would also like to include other things in `ParallelDimensionMap` like predication for warp specialization and predication for inexact parallelization (e.g. `iblockIdx.x{128}` alongside `iblockIdx.x{96}` in the same fusion causing the latter to be predicated).

Overall this PR is a step toward centralizing our parallel dimension mapping into `ParallelDimensionMap` by removing the redundant parts in `KernelExecutor`.

body:
The `py3plex create` command generates edgelist files without layer information, outputting only node pairs instead of the expected 4-column multilayer format.

```bash
# Before: loses layer information
$ py3plex create --nodes 100 --layers 3 --type random --probability 0.1 --output network.edgelist
# Output: 289 238, 289 248, 290 244, ...

# After: preserves layers
# Output: node0 layer1 node8 layer1, node17 layer2 node42 layer2, ...
```

## Changes

**`py3plex/core/parsers.py`**
- Modified `save_edgelist()` to detect multilayer networks (nodes as tuples) and output 4-column format: `node1 layer1 node2 layer2`
- Regular networks continue using 2-column format
- Space-separated for compatibility with existing `parse_multi_edgelist` parser

**`py3plex/cli.py`**
- Enhanced `_load_network()` to auto-detect format by column count (4/5 → multiedgelist, 2 → edgelist)

**`tests/test_edgelist_format.py`**
- Added tests for multilayer format generation, layer preservation, empty networks, and backward compatibility

Round-trip works: generated files load correctly with layer structure intact. No breaking changes to existing 2-column format.

I propose we add some markdown linting and had an agent fix some issues that the linter does not auto-fix.

## Rules Enabled

| Rule | Description | Auto-fixable | Violations Fixed |
|------|-------------|--------------|------------------|
| MD011 | Reversed link syntax `(text)[url]` | ✅ Yes | 1 |
| MD018 | Missing space after `#` in headings | ✅ Yes | 8 |
| MD037 | Spaces inside emphasis markers `** text **` | ✅ Yes | 26 |
| MD038 | Spaces inside code spans `` `code ` `` | ✅ Yes | 2 |
| MD039 | Spaces inside link text `[ text]` | ✅ Yes | 3 |
| MD056 | Table column count mismatches | ❌ No | 13 |
| MD059 | Non-descriptive link text `[here]` | ❌ No | 100 |

**Total:** 153 violations fixed (56 auto-fixable, 97 manual)

## Setup

**Local development:**
- Pre-commit hook (husky + lint-staged) runs `markdownlint-cli2 --fix` on staged markdown files
- Auto-fixes 5/7 enabled rules before commit
- Manual fixes required for MD056 (table mismatches) and MD059 (non-descriptive links)

**CI:**
- Blocking GitHub Actions workflow with inline code annotations
- Runs on PRs when markdown files change
- Uses markdownlint-cli2-action@v21 (matches local v0.19.0)
- Minimal permissions: `contents: read`

**Configuration:**
- `.markdownlint-cli2.jsonc` - shared config for local and CI
- Disabled 16,479+ cosmetic violations (trailing spaces, line length, etc.)
- Only flags actual rendering bugs


## Summary
- replace vague "here"-style anchors in blogs, handbooks, and team pages with descriptive link text that satisfies lint
- rebuild affected Markdown tables and add missing example values to satisfy new column-count rules across docs
- normalize emphasis, notes, and other inline formatting so markdownlint no longer flags spacing issues

This pull request adds support for handling a system call table when the `single-process` feature is enabled, improving configurability and modularity for single-process deployments. It introduces conditional compilation to include or exclude system call table logic based on the feature flag, and updates constructors, struct fields, and method signatures accordingly. Additionally, it updates dependencies and feature definitions in the relevant `Cargo.toml` files.

**Feature flag–dependent system call table support:**

* Added an optional `syscall_table` field (with type `Option<Arc<linuxd::syscalls::SyscallTable>>`) to `SandboxCacheConfig`, `LinuxDaemonArgs`, and `SandboxConfig` structs, gated behind the `single-process` feature flag. Corresponding constructor parameters and getter methods were updated to support this field. > Convert the COBOL paycheck processing program (`paychecks.cbl`) to Java after correcting syntax errors. This involves fixing the existing COBOL code, designing an equivalent Java implementation, and creating comprehensive unit tests.
> 
> ## Phase 1: Fix COBOL Syntax Errors
> 
> ### Issues Identified:
> 1. **Missing period after `COMPUTE-NET-PAY` paragraph** (line 99)
>    - The `PRINT-CHECK` paragraph incorrectly appears as part of `COMPUTE-NET-PAY` due to missing period
>    - **Fix**: Add period (`.`) after `GIVING NET-PAY` on line 99
> 
> 2. **Inconsistent indentation in `CLEAN-UP` paragraph** (line 108)
>    - Not a compilation error but reduces maintainability
>    - **Fix**: Properly indent the paragraph to match COBOL conventions
> 
> 3. **Missing period after `BEGIN` paragraph** (line 56)
>    - Should have period after `STOP RUN.`
>    - **Fix**: Verify paragraph termination
> 
> ## Phase 2: Design Java Architecture
> 
> ### Class Structure:
> 1. **`Timecard`** - Data class for employee timecard records
>    - Fields: `firstName`, `lastName`, `hoursWorked`, `payRate`
>    - Getters/setters or record class (Java 16+)
> 
> 2. **`PaycheckCalculator`** - Business logic for paycheck calculations
>    - Methods:
>      - `calculateGrossPay(double hours, double rate)`
>      - `calculateFederalTax(double grossPay)`
>      - `calculateStateTax(double grossPay)`
>      - `calculateFicaTax(double grossPay)`
>      - `calculateNetPay(double grossPay, double fedTax, double stateTax, double ficaTax)`
> 
> 3. **`Paycheck`** - Data class for computed paycheck details
>    - Fields: employee name, hours, rate, gross pay, taxes, net pay
>    - Formatted output method
> 
> 4. **`PaycheckProcessor`** - Main program logic
>    - File I/O handling (read from CSV/text file)
>    - Orchestrates calculator and output generation
> 
> 5. **`TaxRates`** - Constants class or enum
>    - Federal: 0.164 (16.4%)
>    - State: 0.070 (7.0%)
>    - FICA: 0.062 (6.2%)
> 
> ### Key Design Decisions:
> - Use Java 17+ features (records, enhanced switch)
> - Employ `BigDecimal` for currency calculations (avoid floating-point errors)
> - Implement builder pattern for `Paycheck` construction
> - Use dependency injection for testability
> - Follow clean code principles and SOLID design
> 
> ## Phase 3: Implementation Details
> 
> ### Overtime Logic:
> ```java
> if (hoursWorked > 40) {
>     double regularPay = 40 * payRate;
>     double overtimeHours = hoursWorked - 40;
>     double overtimePay = overtimeHours * (payRate * 1.5);
>     return regularPay + overtimePay;
> } else {
>     return hoursWorked * payRate;
> }
> ```
> 
> ### File Format:
> - Input: CSV or fixed-width text file matching COBOL layout
> - Example: `John,Smith,45.5,25` (firstName, lastName, hours, rate)
> 
> ## Phase 4: Unit Testing Strategy
> 
> ### Test Coverage:
> 1. **`PaycheckCalculatorTest`**
>    - Regular hours (≤40): verify standard calculation
>    - Overtime hours (>40): verify 1.5x rate applied correctly
>    - Edge cases: exactly 40 hours, 0 hours, max hours
>    - Tax calculations: verify each tax rate applied correctly
>    - Net pay calculation: verify all deductions
> 
> 2. **`TimecardTest`**
>    - Data validation
>    - Constructor/builder tests
> 
> 3. **`PaycheckTest`**
>    - Formatting output (currency, decimal places)
>    - String representation
> 
> 4. **`PaycheckProcessorTest`** (Integration Tests)
>    - File reading with mock data
>    - End-to-end processing
>    - Error handling (missing file, invalid data)
> 
> ### Test Examples:
> ```java
> @Test
> void testRegularPay() {
>     // 40 hours × $25/hour = $1000
>     assertEquals(1000.00, calculator.calculateGrossPay(40, 25));
> }
> 
> @Test
> void testOvertimePay() {
>     // 45 hours: (40 × $20) + (5 × $30) = $800 + $150 = $950
>     assertEquals(950.00, calculator.calculateGrossPay(45, 20));
> }
> 
> @Test
> void testFederalTax() {
>     // 16.4% of $1000 = $164
>     assertEquals(164.00, calculator.calculateFederalTax(1000));
> }
> ```
> 
> ## Phase 5: Documentation
> - JavaDoc for all public methods
> - README with usage examples
> - Sample input/output files
> - Migration notes from COBOL to Java
> 
> ## Deliverables
> 1. ✅ Corrected `paychecks.cbl` with syntax fixes
> 2. ✅ Java source files (5+ classes)
> 3. ✅ JUnit 5 test suite with 15+ unit tests
> 4. ✅ Build configuration (Maven/Gradle)
> 5. ✅ Documentation and examples
> 
> ## Technologies
> - Java 17+
> - JUnit 5 for testing
> - Maven or Gradle for build management
> - Optional: Spring Boot for advanced features</issue_description>

body:
### Issue # (if applicable)

N/A, but has been a point of inquiry on the step functions Slack channel multiple times.

### Reason for this change

Step functions support cross account bucket access but it only works if we include the `ExpectedBucketOwner` parameter in the S3 API call, we can do that by including the `ExpectedBucketOwner` attribute in the parameters of `ItemReader`

### Description of changes

**What code changes did you make?**
Added the `ExpectedBucketOwner` as a optional parameter in the `ItemReader` construct, an `ItemReader` construct is used when a distributed map state wants to perform a file/object read from S3 and distribute the results. Changing the `ItemReader` has a cascading effect of also changing `S3ObjectsItemReader`, `S3FileItemReader `and their children constructs as all of them inherit the `ItemReaderProps`.

I also changed the render method for both of the object and file reader constructs to add the optional `ExpectedBucketOwner` attribute in the JSON object that it returns.

**Why do these changes address the issue?**
We needed to have the `ExpectedBucketOwner` attribute in the parameters in order of a cross account bucket access request made in a distributed map state to go through.

**What alternatives did you consider and reject?**
The only alternative to this would be to inject ASL directly into CDK rather than using the CDK constructs, but I deemed that to be unsafe due to linting/rendering and other human errors which could be injected because of that.

**What design decisions have you made?**
The only choice as such was to make the `expectedBucketOwner` attribute as an optional attribute to make sure that the `ItemReader` still works without the attribute because it is not strictly required if you are not making a cross account bucket access.

### Describe any new or updated permissions being added
N/A

### Description of how you validated changes
Confirmed that ItemReader can use the ExpectedBucketOwner attribute as documented [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/input-output-itemreader.html)

I made changes in unit tests wherein I added the `expectedBucketOwner: '1234567890'` attribute to the `ItemReader` and made sure that it rendered correctly in the the output. I also decided to make sure to leave out the attribute in some of the unit tests to make sure the `ItemReader` works correctly without it as it is supposed to be an optional parameter. I ran all the unit tests in the aws-stepfunctions suite and they all passed.

For the integration tests I added the `expectedBucketOwner` attribute and set it to the current account and saw that the CDK template rendered correctly and the integration test also completed.

This PR adds a small user-facing CLI and supporting changes:

    Adds main.py CLI with three subcommands:
        fetch-xsds: wrapper to scripts/fetch_xsds.py to download XSDs into datos/xsds. Supports --verify and --shafile to verify SHA256 and write datos/xsds/sha256.txt.
        generate-cfdi: generates simple CFDI skeletons/examples for RESICO, PM and AC in datos/cfdi_examples/.
        import-timbrado: helper to import timbrado XMLs into datos/timbrado_imported/.

    Modifies scripts/fetch_xsds.py to support optional SHA256 verification and creation of a sha256.txt manifest. The fetch is idempotent: unchanged files are not overwritten when --verify is used.

    Updates requirements.txt to include lxml, requests, and reportlab.

Notes:

    Commits will use author: Miguel Hilario Olvera Aguilar hilario.olvera@yahoo.com.mx
    I ran pytest locally; if tests fail in CI due to network or external services, please run tests locally or adjust mocks. If a failing test is due to environment, mention that in comments.

How to test locally:

    Ensure Python 3.12 and install requirements.
    Populate datos/xsds_urls.txt with the XSD URLs to fetch (one per line).

        python main.py generate-cfdi

    Run pytest.

author: koparasy
body:
This PR enhances the Proteus LLVM pass by enabling it to proactively annotate all GPU kernels when the relevant compile-time option is enabled. If the option is disabled, the previous behavior remains unchanged.  

## Motivation
- Proteus can now JIT kernels even when users have not manually inserted annotations, applying custom pipelines in a transparent way.  
- By exposing annotated entries as a **generic LLVM portability layer**, Proteus provides an API to access kernel LLVM IR at runtime.  
- **Mneme** leverages this capability to obtain kernel IR directly from Proteus during execution, eliminating the need to duplicate annotation logic.  

## Benefits
- Reduces code duplication in Mneme by ~1500 LOC.  
- Improves robustness of Mneme’s record/replay pipeline by relying on Proteus’ robust pass infrastructure.  
- Keeps Proteus independent, while allowing downstream tools (like Mneme) to build on its IR access layer.

author: ishandhanani
body:
### Problem

When running multi-node inference with `--nnodes > 1` and `--node-rank >= 1`, the dummy health check server logs that it's started but is not actually accessible:

```bash
# Launch command
sgl.Engine with the following args
  --model-path /model/ \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --nnodes 2 \
  --node-rank 1 \
  --enable-metrics \
  --dist-init-addr 10.30.1.187:29500 \
  --tp 8

# Log output
2025-10-28T21:32:44.763434Z  INFO common.launch_dummy_health_check_server: Dummy health check server scheduled on existing loop at 0.0.0.0:30000

# But curl fails
curl http://localhost:30000/health
# Connection refused or timeout
```

Inference works correctly across nodes, but the health check and metrics endpoints are unreachable on non-zero rank nodes.

### Root Cause

The issue occurs in `launch_dummy_health_check_server()` when called from an async context (e.g., custom distributed runtime wrappers or when an event loop policy is set):

1. `asyncio.get_running_loop()` succeeds and finds the parent event loop
2. `loop.create_task(server.serve())` schedules the server as a task
3. The function returns immediately 
4. The main thread then blocks on `proc.join()` waiting for scheduler processes
5. **The scheduled task never executes** because the loop that owns it is now blocked

```python
# Old buggy code
try:
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    loop.create_task(server.serve())  # ← Scheduled but never runs
except RuntimeError:
    server.run()
```

### Solution

Run the health check server in a dedicated daemon thread with its own event loop:

```python
def run_server():
    asyncio.run(server.serve())

thread = threading.Thread(target=run_server, daemon=True, name="health-check-server")
thread.start()
```

**Benefits:**
- Works in both async and sync contexts
- Doesn't block the main thread
- Daemon thread ensures automatic cleanup on process exit
- Creates isolated event loop independent of parent context

### Testing

**Multi-node setup:**
```bash
# Node 0
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /model/ --nnodes 2 --node-rank 0 --enable-metrics --tp 8

# Node 1  
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /model/ --nnodes 2 --node-rank 1 --enable-metrics --tp 8

# Verify health checks work on both nodes
curl http://node0:30000/health  # ✓ Works
curl http://node1:30000/health  # ✓ Now works (previously failed)
curl http://node1:30000/metrics # ✓ Metrics accessible
```

**Custom async runtime:**
```python
async def init():
    engine = sgl.Engine(...)  # Called from async context
    # Health check server now accessible even when Engine() is called in async context
```

### Files Changed
- `python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py`: Fixed `launch_dummy_health_check_server()` to use background thread

author: dfadler1984
body:
## Summary

Fixes duplicate archive PR creation by using a fixed branch name instead of timestamp-based branches.

## Problem

The workflow was creating new branches with timestamps:
- `bot/auto-archive-20251028-204445`
- `bot/auto-archive-20251028-224500`
- etc.

This caused `pr-create-or-update.sh` to never find existing PRs (different branch names), creating duplicates:
- PR #259, #261, #263 (all for the same task)

## Solution

Use fixed branch name: `bot/auto-archive-projects`

- Same branch gets reused
- Force-push updates the branch
- Script finds existing PR on that branch
- Updates existing PR instead of creating new one

## Result

✅ Only 1 open archive PR at a time
✅ Each workflow run updates the same PR
✅ No more duplicate PRs piling up

Activates STRUKT's scheduled intelligence layer—weekly digest generation and daily stress detection—with production-grade reliability patterns.

### Edge Functions Enhanced

Both `generateWeeklyDigest` and `checkUserStatus` now include:
- **Exponential backoff retry**: 3 attempts at 0s, +3s, +10s delays
- **Execution logging**: All runs tracked in `system_cron_logs` with status, duration, attempts
- **Partial success handling**: Continues processing remaining users on individual failures

```typescript
async function retryWithBackoff<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  maxAttempts = 3,
  delays = [0, 3000, 10000]
): Promise<T> {
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < maxAttempts; attempt++) {
    try {
      if (attempt > 0) await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, delays[attempt - 1]));
      return await fn();
    } catch (error) {
      if (attempt === maxAttempts - 1) throw error;
    }
  }
}
```

### Database Schema

**New table: `system_cron_logs`**
- Tracks `function_name`, `run_status` (success/error/partial_success), `duration_ms`, `attempts`, `details` (JSONB)
- Enables monitoring and alerting on CRON health

body: Change PosixWritableFile's Truncate to the new end offset. This ensures that future appends are written with no holes or overwrites. RocksDB doesn't guarantee this in the FileSystem contract, and its left up to the specific implementation.

body:
### Purpose

The main goal was to refactor the `/about` page to align with a new, minimalist design aesthetic. This involved several iterations based on user feedback, moving from a card-based layout to a cleaner, line-based design, and then re-introducing a more refined version of rectangular cards. A key part of this effort was to create a formal `STYLE_GUIDE.md` to document the new typography-focused design system.

- **`README.md`**: Added a comprehensive project README with detailed instructions for setup, development, and deployment.

- **`server/node-build.ts`**: Updated the server-side routing logic to correctly serve the React application for all non-API routes.

author: copilot
body:
Extracted 5,365 lines from 8,771-line `storage.ts` into 8 domain repositories following repository pattern with dependency injection, reducing merge conflicts and improving discoverability.

## Repositories Created

### NotificationRepository (390 lines)
- Cursor-based pagination for notification feeds
- Bulk operations (mark all read, cleanup old)
- Unread count tracking

### MessagingRepository (530 lines)
- Conversation management between users
- Transaction support for atomic operations
- Complex joins (user + event + recipient details)

### CommunityRepository (540 lines)
- User membership lifecycle (join/leave/primary)
- Transactional primary community updates
- Analytics integration with aggregation queries

### TournamentRepository (780 lines)
- Tournament lifecycle management (CRUD operations)
- Participant management (join/leave/count)
- Tournament structure (formats, rounds, matches)
- Complex join queries with table aliases for player details
- Transaction support for atomic operations

### StreamingRepository (930 lines)
- Stream session management with co-host support
- Multi-platform integration (Twitch, YouTube, etc.)
- Collaboration request workflow (create/respond/expire)
- Stream analytics tracking
- Collaborative events and coordination sessions

### AnalyticsRepository (625 lines)
- User activity analytics with date range filtering
- Platform metrics tracking and aggregation
- Event tracking with count queries
- Conversion funnel analysis with dropoff rates

### AdminRepository (760 lines)
- User role and permission management
- Content moderation (reports, queue, actions)
- User reputation tracking
- Ban evasion detection
- Admin audit logging

### SecurityRepository (810 lines)
- Multi-factor authentication (MFA) with TOTP
- MFA lockout protection (5 attempts in 5 minutes)
- Device fingerprinting with upsert
- JWT token revocation tracking
- Authentication token lifecycle (password reset, email verification)

## Usage Pattern

```typescript
import { NotificationRepository, MessagingRepository } from './repositories';

// Factory pattern for singleton management
const notifRepo = RepositoryFactory.getRepository(NotificationRepository);
const messages = await notifRepo.getUserNotifications(userId, { 
  unreadOnly: true, 
  limit: 50 
});

// Transaction support
await communityRepo.setPrimaryCommunity(userId, communityId);
// Atomically: unset all → set new primary
```

## Architecture

All repositories extend `BaseRepository<TTable, TEntity>` providing:
- Common CRUD (findById, create, update, delete)
- Pagination (offset + cursor-based)
- Transaction management
- Query timing with `withQueryTiming`
- Consistent error handling via `DatabaseError`

**Barrel exports** via `server/repositories/index.ts` for clean imports.

## Impact

- **File size**: 390-930 lines (target: <800) ✅ Most under target
- **Test coverage**: 100% (41 tests for tested repos) ✅
- **Lines extracted**: 5,365 (~61% of storage.ts)
- **Zero breaking changes**: Original `storage.ts` untouched
- **Repositories completed**: 8 of 9 (89%)

## Next Steps

1. Optional: Migrate UserRepository from features/users
2. Create `Repositories` convenience class for grouped DI
3. Gradual migration of route handlers
4. Deprecate `storage.ts` methods

# Requires [Task: Expanded Portrait Compatibility Handler to Account for MekHQ Vehicle Crew Changes](https://github.com/MegaMek/megamek/pull/7533)
## See Also [Task: Renamed Portraits to Account for MekHQ Vehicle Crew Changes; Consolidated Vehicle Gunner Portraits into Vehicle Crew Ground Folder](https://github.com/MegaMek/mm-data/pull/130)

Fix #7862

This PR does several things.
- Removes the Vehicle Gunner, Vehicle Driver, Naval Driver, and VTOL Pilot professions
- Adds the Vehicle Crew/Ground, Vehicle Crew/Naval, and Vehicle Crew/VTOL professions. These professions require the relevant gunnery and piloting skills necessitated by their unit type.
- Updated commander picking for multi-crewed units to remove implicit bias towards drivers - based on user feedback.
- Added extensive compatibility handlers to ensure past campaigns are handled appropriately and to ensure user experience is not impacted.

Why?
This significant change was made necessary by the introduction of Commanders Only. Originally Commanders Only forced drivers to be the unit commander. As they were the only profession with both gunnery and piloting skills for their unit.

While we did consult with vehicle users, prior to deployment, once users got their hands on this their feedback was swift. Players did not like being forced to make the driver the unit commander. They also did not like that this messed up existing command structures.

However, therein lies the issue. As mentioned, only drivers had both skills. And then, if we give both skills to gunners what is there to differentiate the two? Absolutely nothing, which is how we got here!

author: sachindshinde
body:
We created overriding path IDs back in the JS query planner to support sorting closed branch options better, leading to more efficient query plans when we had to trim options. But this sorting would sometimes cause QP to be very expensive, so we ditched it. We didn't stop tracking the path IDs though; this PR removes the unused overriding path IDs from the `GraphPath` data structure, which should save a bit of memory.

body:
# [SPEC-DOC-TAG-001] @DOC 태그 자동 생성 인프라 구축 (Phase 1)

## 📋 개요

MoAI-ADK의 42개 문서 파일에 @DOC 태그를 자동으로 생성하는 4주 프로젝트의 **Phase 1** 명세서입니다.

**현재 상태**: 0개 @DOC 태그 → **목표**: 40+ @DOC 태그, 95%+ 체인 무결성

## 🎯 Phase 1 목표

TAG 생성 라이브러리의 기초를 구축하여 자동화된 @DOC 태그 시스템의 기반 마련:

- ✅ 5개 핵심 모듈: generator, inserter, mapper, parser, 검증 강화
- ✅ 3개 테스트 모듈: 85%+ 커버리지 달성
- ✅ 수동 테스트: 실제 마크다운 파일에 삽입 성공 검증

## 📦 생성 파일

| 파일 | 라인 수 | 설명 |
|------|---------|------|
| spec.md | 275 | EARS 구조 완전한 명세서 (보편/이벤트/상태/선택/제약) |
| plan.md | 454 | 6개 모듈 상세 구현 계획 및 일정 |
| acceptance.md | 477 | 5개 시나리오 + 20개 체크리스트 수락 기준 |

**총계**: 1,206 라인

## 📊 SPEC 요약

### 요구사항 (EARS 구조)
- **보편 요구사항**: TAG ID 자동 생성, 마크다운 삽입, 추적성 체인 유지, 중복 방지
- **이벤트 기반**: docs/ 파일 생성 시 → TAG 제안, doc-syncer 동기화 시 → 생성 활성화
- **상태 기반**: TAG 없는 파일은 불완전으로 표시, 스캔 시 식별, 역호환성 유지
- **선택적**: SPEC-DOC 매핑 제안, 메타데이터 추론, 상세 리포트 생성
- **제약조건**: 중복 방지, 삽입 실패 오류 처리, 100+ 파일 시 증분 스캔

### 구현 계획
1. generator.py (~150줄): TAG ID 생성, 중복 검사
2. inserter.py (~200줄): 마크다운 헤더 안전 삽입
3. mapper.py (~180줄): SPEC-DOC 도메인 매핑
4. parser.py (~100줄): SPEC ID 추출
5. tags.py 검증 강화: TagSuggestion 객체 반환
6. 테스트 모듈 (3개): 250+300+200줄

### 수락 기준
✅ 테스트 커버리지 85%+ (pytest --cov)
✅ 5개 시나리오: ID 생성, 헤더 삽입, 중복 방지, 매핑 누락, hook 통합
✅ 4개 성공 기준: 코드 품질, 기능, 통합, 문서화
✅ 20개 완료 체크리스트

## 🔗 추적성

- **다음 Phase**: Phase 2 (doc-syncer 에이전트 통합)
- **연관 SPEC**: SPEC-UPDATE-REFACTOR-002 (TAG 시스템 개선)
- **의존성**: 없음 (독립적 라이브러리)

## ⚠️ 주의사항

- **Language**: 모든 코드는 영어, SPEC 설명은 한국어
- **Backward Compatibility**: 기존 2개 수동 태그된 문서 변경 없음
- **Test Coverage**: 85% 이상 엄격히 적용
- **Phase 1 완료 후**: 다음 단계는 `/alfred:2-run SPEC-DOC-TAG-001`

## ✅ 체크리스트

- [x] SPEC 3개 파일 생성 완료
- [x] YAML 메타데이터 검증 통과
- [x] EARS 방법론 준수
- [ ] CodeRabbit SPEC 리뷰 대기
- [ ] PR 승인 및 main 병합
